articles.title: What the Dojo is
articles.summary: A Lorcana sandbox where you play both sides, rewind any turn to try another line, or study a Duels.ink game.
articles.body:
The Practice Dojo is a Lorcana sandbox. You put two decks on the table and play the game out by hand, both sides, at your own pace.

## What you can do

- **Practise a match.** Seat your deck and an opponent's, press **Start match**, and play both players' turns. See [Start your first match](help:first-match).
- **Rewind and try another line.** Every turn you end is saved to the **Multiverse**. Go back to any turn, press **Play from here**, and play it differently. The old line stays. See [What the Multiverse is](help:multiverse).
- **Study a Duels.ink game.** Paste a Duels.ink log or drop a replay file on the home screen, and every turn of that game becomes a turn you can open and replay. See [Study a Duels.ink game](help:import-overview).
- **Practise an opener.** Mulligan with real draw odds, or pick your seven by hand. See [Mulligan and your opening hand](help:mulligan).

## You are the referee

The Dojo keeps the board, counts ink, damage and lore, and saves every turn. It doesn't play for the other side, and it doesn't stop you breaking a rule. For example, you can play a card you can't afford, ink twice in a turn, or challenge with a character that's still drying. When a challenge breaks a rule, the log says so.

## Good to know

- Nothing to install and no account needed. Your sessions and decks are kept in this browser. Signing in is optional.
- Card text and art come from an online card database, so the first visit needs a connection.

articles.title: Start your first match
articles.summary: Seat two decks or paste a list, press Start match, and settle your opening hand.
articles.body:
A match starts on the home screen. Put a deck in each seat under **On the table**, then press **Start match**.

## Seat two decks

**On the table** has two seats. **You** is Player 1 and **Opponent** is Player 2.

- **Pick a built-in or saved deck.** Press one in the deck list under the seats. It goes to the first open seat. With both seats taken, it replaces the opponent. **Your decks** come first. **Default decks** fold away with their heading, and stay folded next time.
- **Find one.** Type in **Find a deck or a card in one**. It matches deck names and the cards in each deck, and it allows typos and missing letters. For example, `lvthn` finds The Leviathan. A deck found by a card names the card and how many copies the deck has. The ink buttons beside the field narrow the list. One ink shows the decks that use it, and two show that exact pair.
- **Paste a decklist.** Paste it into the big field at the top, one card per line, like `4 Tinker Bell - Giant Fairy`. A list copied from Duels.ink, with `(1-193)` after each name, works too. The readout under the field says how many cards it recognised. Press **Play it as you** or **Play against it**, or **Save to My decks** to keep it.
- **Try an example.** With no list to hand, press **A decklist** under the field.

[Show me](show:seats)

Each seat shows the deck's name and card count. The count is marked when it isn't 60. Press **×** on a seat to empty it.

## Start the match

Press **Start match**. Both players draw seven, and Player 1's turn opens on the mulligan. Keep the hand or send cards back. See [Mulligan and your opening hand](help:mulligan).

[Show me](show:start-match)

## Good to know

- **You** is Player 1 and goes first. You play both sides. See [You play both sides](help:you-play-both-sides).
- An empty seat plays 60 random cards.
- Next time, the home screen seats the same saved decks again. A pasted list isn't kept unless you save it.
- The Dojo saves the match to this device as you play. Come back to it from **Pick up again** on the home screen.

articles.title: The screen at a glance
articles.summary: Where everything is on the board, from the top bar and both halves to your hand, ink, lore, deck, discard and the side panels.
articles.body:
The board is split in two. The player whose turn it is sits at the bottom, and the other player sits at the top. When the turn ends, the two halves swap.

## The top bar

:::desktop
- **Left.** **‹ Dojo** goes back to the home screen. Next come the session's title, which you click to rename, then **Save**, **Save as copy** and **Share**.
- **Centre.** **Undo**, the turn chip and **Challenge**. The turn chip reads like `TURN 16 → Player 2`.
- **Right.** **Multiverse** and **Tweaks**.
:::

:::phone
From left to right, the bar holds **☰** for the side panel, **Undo**, the turn chip, **Challenge**, **Multiverse** and **⋯**. The **⋯** menu holds **Save**, **Save as copy**, **Share link**, **Tweaks** and **Leave to the dojo**.
:::

[Show me](show:topbar)

## Each player's half

:::desktop
Each half is labelled `P1 · TO PLAY` or `P2 · WAITING`. It holds these parts:

- **The play area**, where characters, items and locations sit.
- **Discard**, a list of the cards in it, with a magnifier to look through them.
- **The ink bar**, with the ready ink count, **−** and **+**, **Ready all** and the ink cards. The count reads like `4 /7 READY`.
- **Deck**, with its count. Click it to draw.
- **Lore**, the big number, with **−** and **+**.

The bottom half also has your hand and the **Turn N notes** box. The top half has the other player's hand face down, with **Hold to Reveal Hand**.
:::

:::phone
Each player has one bar. It holds **Lore** with **−** and **+**, then **Ink** with its count and pips, then the discard with its top card and count, then the deck. Tap **Ink** for the inkwell. Tap the deck to draw, or **⋮** for more. Under the board, the hand tray holds **Quest**, `Hand · N` and **End turn**, and your hand peeks up from the bottom edge.
:::

[Show me](show:board)

## The side panels

:::desktop
The left rail holds the players with their deck and hand counts, the mini multiverse, the lore race, the card preview, the game log, **Auto-save every turn**, **Quest** and **End turn**. Hover a card to see its details in the card preview. The right pane shows **Draw Odds** for the player to play.
:::

:::phone
**☰** opens the side panel. It holds the players, the card preview, the game log, **Auto-save every turn**, **Quest** and **End turn**. Phones have no draw odds pane, mini multiverse, lore race or notes box. To write a note on a phone, see [Turn notes](help:turn-notes).
:::

[Show me](show:sidebar)

## Good to know

- The colour of a half follows the player, not the position. Player 1 keeps their colour when they move to the top.
- On a phone or tablet, tap a card to open the card drawer with all its actions. See [Act on a card in play](help:card-actions).

articles.title: You play both sides
articles.summary: You take both players' turns, and the board shows whose turn it is.
articles.body:
You play Player 1's turn, end it, then play Player 2's turn, and so on. That's how you test a line against the best answer you can think of. The beta rules engine can play the other side for you. See [Play against the bot](help:bot-opponent).

## Whose turn it is

The turn chip in the top bar names the player to play, for example `TURN 3 → Player 2`. The player to play always sits on the **bottom** half of the board, labelled `TO PLAY`. The other player sits at the top, labelled `WAITING`.

[Show me](show:turn)

When you end the turn, the halves swap. The other player moves to the bottom and their turn begins. See [End your turn](help:end-turn).

## The other player's hand

The waiting player's hand is face down at the top of the board.

:::desktop
Hold **Hold to Reveal Hand** to see it, and let go to hide it again.
:::

:::phone
Tap **Hold to Reveal Hand** to show it, and tap again to hide it.
:::

The log notes each peek. The hand hides again when the turn ends.

## Good to know

- You can still act on the waiting player's cards. You can damage them, banish them, change their lore or draw for them.
- The sidebar lists **Player 1 (You)** and **Player 2**. "You" is the seat that goes first.

articles.title: Guided tours
articles.summary: Short tours that point at the real controls on a practice board. Nothing you do in a tour is saved.
articles.body:
A guided tour points at the real controls one at a time and waits while you try each one. There are four tours, and each takes a few minutes:

- **Your first turn** covers the mulligan, the board, inking and playing a card, reading a card, ending the turn, playing the other side, [Undo](help:undo) and where to find the [Multiverse](help:multiverse).
- **You're the referee** opens a game in progress where you carry out the cards' effects yourself. You draw for **The Horseman Strikes!** and pick the character with Evasive. The Dojo lets you pick the wrong one. Then you put actions in the discard, quest, exert, return a character to your hand, shift, challenge, and set lore by hand.
- **The Multiverse** runs on a copy of the Set 14 demo. You open the Multiverse, read and select a node, press **Play from here**, and see branches, saving the turn you're in and the plot view. It ends with the mini map on desktop or the thumb keys on a phone.
- **Study a Duels.ink game** covers the paste field, the example log, the readout, **Study this game** and the imported turns in the Multiverse.

## Start a tour

:::desktop
Open Help with the **?** in the top bar, or press {key:?}. The tours are at the top of the list. A ✓ marks the ones you've finished.
:::

:::phone
Open Help from the **⋯** menu, or press **Help** on the home screen. The tours are at the top of the list. A ✓ marks the ones you've finished.
:::

The first time you open the Dojo, a welcome offers the first tour. Press **Start the tour**, or press **Explore on my own** and it won't ask again. Your first **Start match** asks once more, unless you've done *Your first turn*. **Take the tour first** starts your match, runs the tour, then brings you back to the match. **Just play** starts the match without the tour. Until you first open Help, its button pulses orange.

## During a tour

- Each step names the control to use. Steps that wait for you have **Skip this step**. The other steps have **Next** and **Back**.
- **Learn more** opens the article for that step. Close Help and the tour carries on.

:::desktop
Leave any time with the **✕** on the tour card, or press {key:Esc}.
:::

:::phone
Leave any time with the **✕** on the tour card.
:::

## Good to know

- A tour plays on a practice board, marked **Practice · not saved**. Nothing you do there goes in your library. The match you had open waits, unchanged, until the tour ends.
- To keep the practice board, press **Save a copy** in its banner. It makes the board a session of your own and ends the tour.
- Reloading the page ends a tour. Start it again from Help.

articles.title: Mulligan and your opening hand
articles.summary: Each player's first turn opens on their mulligan. Keep the seven, or mark cards to send to the bottom and draw again.

headings.text: Read the hand before you choose

articles.body:
Each player's first turn opens on the mulligan. Player 1 chooses as the match starts. Player 2 chooses when Player 1 ends their first turn, before Player 2's draw, so they choose from the seven they were dealt.

## Keep or send cards back

The dialog shows your seven, cheapest first. The head says whether you're **on the play** or **on the draw**. On the play, you don't draw on turn 1. On the draw, you draw one card once you've chosen.

:::desktop
Click a card to mark it to go to the bottom, and click it again to unmark it. To read a card, click the magnifier in its corner, and the card grows in place. Any click or {key:Esc} puts it back.
:::

:::phone
Tap a card to mark it to go to the bottom, and tap it again to unmark it. To read a card, {gesture:long-press} it. It shows large with its name, cost and type. Tap anywhere to close it. That tap marks nothing.
:::

A marked card sinks and shows `↓ Bottom`. Then press the one button at the foot:

- **Keep hand** shows when nothing is marked. The hand stays and the deck isn't touched.
- **Mulligan N cards** shows otherwise. The marked cards go to the bottom of the deck, you draw as many from the top, and then the Dojo shuffles the deck.

[Show me](show:mulligan-confirm)

## Read the hand before you choose

The readout under the hand follows your marks. It has three parts:

- **Curve** shows the cards you'd keep. The cards going back show dashed.
- **Inkable** counts the cards you'd keep that can be inked.
- The plan counts kept cards and redraws, for example `5 kept + 2 redraw`.

**Draw odds** show your chance to find each card. **RD** is the chance among the redraws, and the next columns are the chances within the next turns' draws. Phones show the top three rows. Press **All** for the rest.

[Show me](show:mulligan-readout)

## After a mulligan

The dialog stays open on your new hand. The new cards carry a **NEW** tag, and the readout says how many cards went back and how many you drew. You can't mark cards again. Press **Start turn**, or **Draw and start turn** for Player 2, to play.

## Good to know

- Nothing else works until the hand is settled. Hotkeys don't fire, and the turn can't end.
- **Build** and **Replay**, next to **Draw** at the top, make the hand another way. **Build** lets you pick your seven, and **Replay** copies an opening from a saved game. See [Build or replay an opening hand](help:craft-hand).
- **Undo** after the turn has started brings the mulligan back.
- **×** at the top right, or {key:Esc}, leaves for the home screen. The match stays saved, still on its mulligan. **Back to match** or **Resume** brings the dialog back. [Show me](show:mulligan-leave)

articles.title: Build or replay an opening hand
articles.summary: Pick your seven from the whole deck, or replay the exact hand and deck order of an opening from a saved game.
articles.body:
The opening-hand dialog makes your hand in three ways. The switch at its top picks one. **Draw** deals seven and offers the mulligan. **Build** lets you pick the seven yourself. **Replay** copies an opening from another game. The dialog always opens on **Draw**.

## Build your seven

Pick an opener card by card to practise it again and again.

1. When your mulligan opens, press **Build**. [Show me](show:craft-hand)
2. Your hand is in the middle, as seven empty slots. Your deck is on the right, or below the hand on a phone, cheapest first. The dots under a card count its copies. A filled dot is a copy in your hand.
3. Click or tap a card in the deck to put it in the next slot. Click a card in your hand to take it out.
4. **Find a card** searches by name. On desktop, the cost buttons show one cost at a time.
5. **Fill the rest at random** fills the empty slots from the rest of the deck. A phone labels it **Random**. Pick the two cards you care about and let the rest be random.
6. When all seven are in, press **Keep this hand**. The Dojo shuffles the rest of the deck and your turn starts. Player 2 draws for the turn first, as usual.

## Replay an opening

Replay copies another game's opening. You get the same seven in hand and the same deck order underneath, so you see the same draws. Use it to test whether another line, or another deck, beats the draws a deck had.

1. When your mulligan opens, press **Replay**. [Show me](show:replay-opening)
2. The list shows every opening in your saved games on this device, then in the demos, grouped by game. Each one names its deck, says whether it was on the play or the draw, and says how the hand was settled, such as **kept**, **mull 2** or **built**. The list leaves out the game on the board and Duels.ink imports. An import doesn't know the hidden deck order.
3. **Your deck** shows only openings of the deck you have here. **All** shows every deck. **Find a game or deck** searches the list.
4. Pick an opening. Its seven cards show in the middle with their curve. **Your next draws** shows the next four cards, labelled by the turn you'd draw them on. On a phone the opening opens by itself, and **Openings** goes back to the list.
5. Press **Play this opening**. If you go second, you still draw your top card for the turn. If you go first, you don't.

If the opening is from a different deck, the button says **Switch deck and play** and the line beside it names the deck you get. Your opponent's deck stays as it is.

## Good to know

- Replay copies only the opening. Shuffles later in the game are random again.
- An older game whose deck was shuffled or reordered on turn 1 can't give back its order. That opening shows greyed out.
- The log and the turn's recap say where a replayed opening came from.
- Building or replaying takes the place of the mulligan. Once you keep the hand, it's settled. **Undo** brings the mulligan back.

articles.title: Drawing cards
articles.summary: The player to play draws one card when their turn begins. Draw more from the deck at any time.
articles.body:
The player to play draws one card when their turn begins. Player 1 doesn't draw on their first turn.

## Draw another card

:::desktop
Click the deck slab on that player's half. The card goes to their hand. You can also drag the top card of the deck to the hand, the play area or the ink bar.
:::

:::phone
Tap the deck on that player's bar. The card goes to their hand.
:::

[Show me](show:deck)

This works for either player's deck. A card effect that makes the other player draw takes one click.

## Good to know

- The log records extra draws, and the turn's **Drawn** recap counts them.
- An empty deck doesn't draw. The Dojo doesn't end the game for it.
- To look through the deck or shuffle it, use the deck's other controls. See [Look through your deck](help:inspect-deck).
- **Undo** puts a drawn card back.

articles.title: Ink a card
articles.summary: Put a card from your hand into your inkwell, face down, to pay for cards later.

headings.text: See what you inked this turn

articles.body:
Ink a card to grow your inkwell. Ink pays for the cards you play. A card goes in ready, so you can spend it the turn you ink it.

## Ink a card

:::desktop
Drag a card from your hand onto your ink bar. Any part of the bar takes it. You can also hover the card and press **INK**, or click it and choose **Add to Inkwell**.
:::

:::phone
Tap the card in your hand. In the card drawer, press **Ink**. You can also drag the card up onto the ink count on your player bar.
:::

[Show me](show:ink-bar)

## See what you inked this turn

A card inked this turn shows face up in the inkwell, and the count gets a tag. The tag reads **+1** on desktop and **+1 inked** on a phone. Until you ink, a phone's bar says **No ink yet**. The cards turn face down when that player's next turn begins.

## Good to know

- The Dojo doesn't enforce one ink a turn. The tag shows how many cards you've inked.
- **INK**, **Add to Inkwell** and **Ink** only appear for a card with the inkwell symbol. A phone shows **No ink** instead. Dragging doesn't check, so you can ink any card.
- To take it back, press **Undo**, or move the ink card to your hand. See [Your inkwell](help:inkwell).

articles.title: Your inkwell: ready, spend, ready all
articles.summary: Read your ready ink, spend or ready it by hand, and act on a single ink card.
articles.body:
Your inkwell shows how much ink you have ready out of your total. Playing a card spends ink for you. Use these controls for everything else, such as an ability that costs ink.

## Read your ink

:::desktop
The ink bar reads like `4 /7 READY`, which means four ready out of seven. Spent ink cards are dimmed and turned. The ink cards sit on the right of the bar, and overlap once they don't fit.
:::

:::phone
Your player bar shows a count like `4/7` and a pip for each ink. A spent ink's pip is dimmed.
:::

[Show me](show:ink-bar)

## Spend or ready ink

:::desktop
On the ink bar, **−** spends one ink, **+** readies one, and **Ready all** readies all of them.
:::

:::phone
Tap the ink count to open the inkwell. **−** spends one, **+** readies one, and **Ready all** readies all of them. **×** or a tap outside closes it.
:::

## Act on one ink card

:::desktop
Click an ink card. It opens in place with **Exert** or **Ready**, **To hand** and **Discard**. Click it again, click elsewhere or press {key:Esc} to put it down.
:::

:::phone
In the inkwell, tap an ink card. Then press **Exert** or **Ready**, **To hand** or **Discard** in the bar underneath.
:::

[Show me](show:ink-panel)

## Ink drops

When a card in either deck mentions ink drops, each player gets an ink drops counter, kept apart from their ink. Hyperia City is one such card. Without such a card, the counter doesn't show.

:::desktop
The **Ink drops** box sits in the ink bar, left of the deck. **−** and **+** change the count.
:::

:::phone
The teardrop count sits in your player bar, between your ink and your piles. **−** and **+** change it. The ink pips hide to make room, and the `ready/total` count stays.
:::

## Good to know

- Both players' inkwells work the same way, so you can fix the waiting player's ink too.
- Ink readies by itself at the start of that player's turn.
- If you play a card you can't afford, the Dojo spends no ink. Spend it by hand with **−** if you need to.

articles.title: Play a card
articles.summary: Move a card from your hand onto the field. The Dojo spends the ink for you.
articles.body:
Play a card from your hand to put it into play. If you have enough ready ink, the Dojo spends the card's cost for you.

## Play a card

:::desktop
Drag the card from your hand onto your play area. Any part of the area takes it. You can also hover the card and press **PLAY**, or click it and choose **Play Card (-3 Ink)**.
:::

:::phone
Tap the card in your hand to open the card drawer. It shows the cost and your ready ink. Press **Play · −3 ink**. You can also drag the card up onto the board.
:::

[Show me](show:hand)

A character comes in **drying**. It shows a **NEW** tag and can't quest until your next turn. Songs and actions also land in play. When they're done, banish them to send them to the discard.

## Not enough ink

You can still play the card. The Dojo plays it and spends no ink, so you can test a line you can't quite afford. On a phone the key shows the shortfall, for example **Play anyway · 2 short**.

## Good to know

- To shift a card or play a character straight to a location, drag it onto that card instead. See [Locations, shift and cards under](help:locations-and-stacks).
- Card abilities don't trigger by themselves. Do what the card says by hand, such as drawing, adding damage or changing lore.
- **Undo** takes the play back, ink included.

articles.title: Act on a card in play (exert, ready, damage, banish)
articles.summary: Exert and ready, add or remove damage, banish, and the hover hotkeys for each.
articles.body:
You can exert or ready every card in play on either side of the board, add or remove its damage, and banish it. Pick whichever way suits your device.

## Hover controls

:::desktop
Point at a card in play. A damage stepper appears on top, showing **−** `0/3` **+**. A column of icon buttons appears down the card's right edge. Hover a button to see its name. The buttons are these:

- **Challenge** and **Quest**, on your characters when they can.
- **Exert** or **Ready**.
- **Modify**, which adds a [modifier](help:modifiers).
- **Banish**.

On a small card the buttons wrap into two columns.

Under every card with willpower sits a track with one segment per point. Click a segment to set the damage exactly. Click the lit end segment to take one off.
:::

## Hover hotkeys

:::desktop
These keys act on the card under the pointer:

| Key | Does |
|---|---|
| {key:+} / {key:-} | add or remove one damage |
| {key:0} to {key:9} | set the damage to that number |
| {key:E} | exert or ready |
| {key:B} | banish |
| {key:C} | challenge mode, with this character picked |
:::

## The card menu

:::desktop
Right-click or click a card in play for its menu. Only what applies to that card shows. The menu has these groups:

- **Card** holds **Exert** or **Ready**, **Quest (+2 Lore)**, **Challenge…**, **Leave Location**, and a **Damage** stepper that stays open while you click it.
- **Modifiers** holds **Add Modifier…**, and **Remove …** for each modifier the card has.
- **Move** holds **Banish (To Discard)**, **Return to Hand**, **Put on Top of Deck** and **Put on Bottom of Deck**.
- **Stack** holds **Put Top Card of Deck Under** and **Separate Stacked Cards**.

To use the menu without a mouse, turn on **Number keys** in [Tweaks](help:tweaks). Press {key:B} then a number to open the menu of that card on your battlefield, counting from the left. The menu numbers its first nine options. Press {key:1} to {key:9} to choose one. See [Keyboard shortcuts](help:keyboard-shortcuts).
:::

## The card drawer

:::touch
Tap a card in play to open the card drawer. The head names the card's player and its state, for example `P2 · exerted · 2 / 5`. Under the card's text are these controls:

- **Damage.** Tap a segment to set it, or press **− 1** or **+ 1**.
- **Challenge**, **Quest**, **Exert** or **Ready**, and **Banish**. A key you can't use is hollow.
- **Modifiers.** The card's modifiers and **+ Add modifier**. Tap a modifier to remove it. See [Modifiers](help:modifiers).
- **Move to.** **To hand**, **Deck top**, **Deck bottom** and **Put under**, plus **Leave location** or **Separate stack** when they apply.

Step to the next card in play with **‹ ›** or a sideways {gesture:swipe} on the text. **×**, a tap outside or {key:Esc} closes the drawer.
:::

[Show me](show:field)

## Good to know

- Once damage reaches willpower, the card pulses and shows a **LETHAL · BANISH** button under it. The drawer says `lethal`. The Dojo doesn't banish the card until you do, except after a challenge.
- A banished card goes to its owner's discard with any cards under it, and its damage is cleared.
- The Dojo doesn't check card effects. Exert, ready or damage anything the cards say to.
- **Undo** takes back every change.

articles.title: Quest and lore
articles.summary: Quest with one character or all of them, and change lore by hand.
articles.body:
Questing exerts a character and adds its lore to its player's score. The first player to reach 20 lore wins.

## Quest with one character

:::desktop
Hover the character and press the quest button, which shows the lore gem. You can also click the character and choose **Quest (+2 Lore)**.
:::

:::touch
Tap the character, then press **Quest** in the card drawer.
:::

A character can quest when it belongs to the player to play, is ready, isn't drying and has lore.

## Quest with everyone

Press **Quest** and every ready, dry character with lore quests at once. The number beside the button says how many will quest. {key:Q} does the same on a keyboard.

:::desktop
**Quest** sits at the foot of the left rail, above **End turn**.
:::

:::phone
**Quest** sits in the hand tray, left of your hand.
:::

[Show me](show:quest-all)

## Change lore by hand

Press **−** or **+** beside a player's **Lore** to take one off or add one. Use it for lore from abilities and locations, or to fix a mistake. Lore never goes below 0.

[Show me](show:lore)

## Good to know

- Quest uses the lore printed on the card plus any lore [modifiers](help:modifiers) on it. For other bonuses from abilities, add the lore with **+**.
- The Dojo doesn't check the quest restrictions printed on cards. You check them.
- The log notes lore changed by hand, and **Undo** takes any of it back.
- At 20 lore the Dojo names the winner. See [Winning a game](help:winning).

articles.title: Challenge
articles.summary: Challenge an opposing card by dragging or tapping, with a forecast of what happens before you commit.
articles.body:
In a challenge, your character and the opposing card deal their strength to each other as damage. The Dojo works out the damage, exerts your character and banishes any card whose damage reaches its willpower. It counts [modifiers](help:modifiers) on either card, such as +strength, Challenger, Resist and willpower.

## Challenge mode

Press **Challenge** in the top bar, or press {key:C}. A bar across the board reads **CHALLENGE MODE**.

:::desktop
Drag one of your characters onto an opposing card. You can also click your character, then click the target. With a character picked, hovering a target shows the forecast.

The arrow keys work like the phone's thumb keys. The first arrow picks your first ready character, and {key:←} {key:→} {key:↑} {key:↓} step through your characters. {key:↑} off your top row moves to the opponent's cards. The arrows then aim at a target, which lights up, and a red arrow runs to it with the forecast. Press {key:Enter} to challenge. {key:↓} off their bottom row goes back to your characters.
:::

:::touch
Tap one of your characters, then tap an opposing card. Once you've picked, every opposing card shows a badge with the outcome. Dragging also works.
:::

:::phone
Thumb keys sit at the bottom right of your side, like the Multiverse's. The mode starts on your first ready character. ◀ ▶ ▲ ▼ step through your characters. The swap key, or ▲ off your top row, moves to the opponent's cards. The arrows then aim, and a red arrow runs from your character to the target. Press the fist to challenge. Press swap again to go back to your characters. Tapping also works. Tap an opposing card to aim at it, and tap it again to challenge.

A tap on the bare battlefield leaves challenge mode.
:::

You stay in the mode to challenge again. Press **Done** to leave. The first {key:Esc} drops the picked character, and the second leaves. Ending the turn also leaves the mode.

[Show me](show:challenge-mode)

## Start from a character

:::desktop
Hover your character and press its challenge button, or right-click it and choose **Challenge…**. Challenge mode opens with it picked. You can also drag your character onto an opposing card without entering the mode. That works on a character standing at a location and on the location itself.
:::

:::touch
Tap your character and press **Challenge** in the card drawer. Challenge mode opens with it picked. Tap the target.
:::

## The forecast

Before you commit, the Dojo shows each card's damage after the challenge and whether it's banished, with labels such as **✕ Banishes …** and **⇄ Trade**. Choose how much it shows with **Off**, **Light** or **Full** in the challenge bar. See [Challenge forecast](help:forecast).

## Good to know

- Damage is strength, plus **Challenger +N** on the challenger, minus **Resist +N** on the card taking it. Only a card's own printed Challenger and Resist count. An ability may give them to another character, as in "give chosen character Resist +2", or only under a condition, as in "while you have no cards in your hand". Add those as a [modifier](help:modifiers) when they apply. The Dojo doesn't apply other abilities. Fix damage by hand afterwards.
- The Dojo doesn't stop an exerted or drying challenger, or a ready target. It allows them and notes it in the log.
- The Dojo doesn't check Bodyguard, Evasive and similar keywords. You're the referee.
- One **Undo** takes back the whole challenge.

articles.title: Modifiers (+strength, Challenger, Resist)
articles.summary: Give a card in play more or less strength, willpower or lore, or Challenger +X or Resist +X, for this turn, until your next turn, or for good.
articles.body:
Card effects often change a character for a while. Examples are "+2 strength this turn", "gains Resist +1 until the start of your next turn" and "Challenger +3". Add these as modifiers. The Dojo counts them in challenges and quests, then takes them off when they end.

## Add a modifier

:::desktop
Point at a card in play and press its **Modify** button, which shows a plus and minus icon. You can also right-click the card and choose **Add Modifier…**.
:::

:::touch
Tap a card in play and press **+ Add modifier** in the card drawer.
:::

In the picker, choose these:

1. **Stat.** Pick **STR**, **WP**, **LORE**, **Challenger** or **Resist**.
2. **Amount.** Set it with **−** and **+**. Strength, willpower and lore can go down. Challenger and Resist only go up.
3. **Lasts.** Pick **This turn**, **Until my next turn** or **Always**.

Press **Add** or {key:Enter}. Tick **All of P1's characters** to give every character that player has in play the same modifier. Use it for songs and effects that hit them all. **Recent** keeps your last four modifiers as one-tap buttons, and the picker opens on the last one you used.

:::desktop
The picker stays open after each add, so you can give a card several modifiers or move on to another card. Press {key:←} or {key:→} to move it to the next character or location in the same battlefield. It wraps round and skips items. Press {key:↑} or {key:↓} to jump to your opponent's battlefield or yours. The card it points at is outlined. Your stat, amount and duration stay as they were. Click anywhere else, press the **×**, or press {key:Esc} to close it.
:::

:::touch
On a phone the picker is a sheet that closes after each add.
:::

## How long it lasts

- **This turn** ends when the turn ends.
- **Until my next turn** lasts through your opponent's whole turn and ends when your next turn starts. "My" means the player whose turn it was when you added the modifier.
- **Always** stays until you remove it or the card leaves play.

The log lists each modifier as it ends. A card that leaves play loses its modifiers. A character you shift onto keeps them.

## On the card

Each modifier is a pill on the card's left edge, such as `+2 STR`, `RES +1` or `CHAL +3`. The card keeps its printed numbers, and the pills show what's added. The pill's colour says how long it lasts:

- Red-orange means this turn.
- Teal means until my next turn.
- Olive means always.

A plus is a filled pill. A minus is hollow, with a coloured edge and text. The same colours mark the choices in the picker.

## Remove a modifier

:::desktop
Click its pill on the card, or right-click the card and choose **Remove …** under **Modifiers**.
:::

:::touch
Open the card drawer and tap the pill under **Modifiers**.
:::

**Undo** brings it back.

## What they change

- **Challenges.** The Dojo first adds up the challenger's printed strength, its strength modifiers and Challenger, and only the total stops at 0. So a 0-strength character with −2 strength and Challenger +2 deals 0, not 2. The defender's Resist comes off that total. The damage back works the same way, in the result and the forecast. The card's own printed Challenger and Resist still count, and modifiers add to them.
- **Quests.** Modifiers change the lore that a quest and **Quest all** gain, and which characters count as able to quest.
- **Willpower.** Modifiers change the damage track, the lethal warning, and banishing after a challenge.

articles.title: Locations, shift and cards under
articles.summary: Move characters to a location, shift onto a character, put cards under, and separate a stack.

headings.text: Move a character to a location

articles.body:
Locations sit in your play area, with the characters at each location above it. Shift and "put under" build a stack, with one card on top and the rest underneath.

## Move a character to a location

Drag the character onto the location. A character dragged from your hand is played straight to the location, and the Dojo spends its cost.

To leave, choose **Leave Location** in the card's menu on desktop or **Leave location** in the card drawer on touch. You can also drag the character back onto an empty part of your play area.

:::touch
Dragging also works on touch screens. Press the card, then move it.
:::

## Shift onto a character

Drag the new card from your hand onto the character it shifts onto. It goes on top and keeps the lower card's damage, exerted state and location. The log records the shift. The badge in the corner counts the cards under it.

You can drop any of your cards onto another of yours this way. Only a card with a matching name counts as a shift.

## Put a card under

:::desktop
Right-click your card and choose **Put Top Card of Deck Under**. The deck's top card goes under it face down.
:::

:::touch
Tap your card and press **Put under** in the card drawer.
:::

## Separate a stack

Choose **Separate Stacked Cards** in the menu, or **Separate stack** in the drawer. The cards underneath come out into play, exerted and drying.

[Show me](show:field)

## Good to know

- When you drag a character from your hand onto another character, the Dojo spends its Shift cost if that cost is in ink, as in **Shift 5** or **Universal Shift 4**. If you don't have that much ready ink, it spends none. A Shift paid another way, such as **Shift: Discard a card**, spends no ink, so pay it by hand. Any other card dragged from your hand spends its full cost.
- Moving to a location costs nothing in the Dojo. Spend the move cost with **−** on your ink bar.
- The Dojo doesn't add a location's lore at the start of your turn. Add it with the lore **+**.
- When a card with cards under it leaves play, the cards under it go with it.
- If you banish a location, the characters at it stay in play.

articles.title: Move cards: to hand, deck top or bottom, discard
articles.summary: Send any card back to the hand, the top or bottom of the deck, or the discard.
articles.body:
Card effects often move cards between zones. Any card in play or in a hand can go back to the hand, onto the top or bottom of the deck, or into the discard.

## From play

:::desktop
Right-click the card. The **Move** group holds **Banish (To Discard)**, **Return to Hand**, **Put on Top of Deck** and **Put on Bottom of Deck**.
:::

:::touch
Tap the card. In the card drawer, press **Banish**, or pick **To hand**, **Deck top** or **Deck bottom** under **Move to**.
:::

## From a hand

:::desktop
Right-click the card in your hand and choose **Discard Card**, **Put on Top of Deck** or **Put on Bottom of Deck**.
:::

:::phone
Tap the card in your hand. In the card drawer, press **Discard**, or pick **Deck top** or **Deck bottom** under **More**.
:::

## By dragging

:::desktop
Drag a card onto a deck, a discard pile or a hand. A card dropped on a deck goes on top. Dragging works from play, a hand or the inkwell.
:::

[Show me](show:field)

## Good to know

- A card leaving play loses its damage and exert, and takes any cards under it along.
- The menu and the drawer send a card to its own player's deck, hand or discard. A drag puts the card where you drop it.
- An ink card can go from the inkwell to the hand or the discard. See [Your inkwell](help:inkwell).
- To bring a card back from the discard, see [Your discard pile](help:inspect-discard).
- **Undo** takes any move back.

articles.title: End your turn
articles.summary: End the turn. With auto-save on, the Dojo saves it to the Multiverse, then the other player readies and draws.
articles.body:
When you're done, end the turn. The other player's turn begins, and the board swaps so they're at the bottom.

## End the turn

:::desktop
Press **End turn →** at the foot of the left rail, or press {key:Space}.
:::

:::phone
Press **End turn** in the hand tray, right of your hand. The **☰** panel also has it.
:::

[Show me](show:end-turn)

## What happens next

1. The other player becomes the player to play. The turn number goes up when Player 1's turn comes round.
2. **Ready step.** Their characters and items ready, drying ends, and their ink readies. Cards they inked last turn turn face down. Locations don't ready.
3. **Draw step.** They draw a card.
4. **Auto-save.** The node of the turn you ended gets your turn note and a recap of what you drew, inked, played, quested and banished. The new turn gets its own node, named like `Turn 4 - Player 1 Active`. See [Every turn is saved](help:auto-save).

Challenge mode ends, and the other player's hand is hidden again.

## Auto-save every turn

The **Auto-save every turn** switch sits in the left rail, or in the **☰** panel on a phone. It's on by default. Turn it off and ending the turn saves no node.

[Show me](show:auto-save)

## Good to know

- Player 2's first turn opens on their mulligan, and their draw comes after it. See [Mulligan](help:mulligan).
- The turn can't end while a mulligan is open.
- The Dojo doesn't apply abilities that trigger at the start or end of a turn. Do them by hand.
- If you ended the turn too soon, **Undo** takes you back. The node it saved stays in the Multiverse.

articles.title: Undo
articles.summary: Take back the last action, as many steps as you like.
articles.body:
**Undo** takes back your last action. Press it again to keep going back, one action at a time.

## Undo an action

:::desktop
Press **Undo** in the top bar, beside the turn chip. The round-arrow button at the foot of the rail does the same.
:::

:::phone
Press the round-arrow button in the top bar, left of the turn chip.
:::

[Show me](show:undo)

## What it covers

Undo covers everything you do on the board. That includes playing, inking, moving and drawing cards, damage, exert and ready, quests and challenges, lore, ink, turn notes, the mulligan and ending the turn. The log steps back with it.

Undo goes back up to 250 actions. The session keeps the history, so Undo still works after you leave and come back.

## Good to know

- There's no redo. To try both versions of a turn, save the turn first and branch in the Multiverse. See [Branching](help:branches).
- Undo doesn't change the Multiverse. A node saved when you ended a turn stays. Ending the turn again saves a new node beside it.
- **Play from here** in the Multiverse, or a jump on the mini multiverse, starts a fresh undo history.
- {key:U} also undoes, while you're not typing in a field.

articles.title: Turn notes
articles.summary: Write a note for the turn you're in. It goes with the turn into the Multiverse.
articles.body:
Write down what you're trying, or why, as you play. Each player has one note per turn, and the Dojo saves it with that turn's node in the Multiverse.

## Write a note

:::desktop
Type in the **Turn N notes** box at the bottom left of the board. It saves when you click away.
:::

:::phone
{gesture:long-press} an empty part of the board. A **Turn N notes** dialog opens with the note for the player to play. Press **Save**, or press **Cancel** to leave it as it was. {key:Enter} adds a line, and {key:Ctrl+Enter} saves.
:::

[Show me](show:turn-notes)

The note shows in the game log under its turn, as **Turn N note · Player N**.

## Where the note goes

When the turn ends with auto-save on, the note goes into the new node, above the recap of the turn. **Save current unfinished turn** in the Multiverse also starts its note from it. To change a note later, edit it in the Multiverse panel. See [The Multiverse panel](help:multiverse-panel).

## Good to know

- The note belongs to the player to play and the turn number. The other player's turn starts with an empty box.
- Hotkeys don't fire while you type in the notes box.
- Saving an empty note clears it.

articles.title: Winning a game (20 lore)
articles.summary: At 20 lore the branch is won. The Dojo says so and offers the Multiverse to try other lines.
articles.body:
The first player to reach 20 lore wins. The Dojo notices whether the lore came from a quest, **Quest** or the lore **+**.

## When a player reaches 20

A dialog names the winner, the lore score and the turn. The Dojo saves a **Game Over - Player 1 Wins!** node to the Multiverse, whether auto-save is on or not. Then choose one of these:

- **View Multiverse** shows the game as a tree, where you pick another turn to replay.
- **Stay Here** keeps you playing on this board.

[Show me](show:lore)

## Try another line

A win ends one branch, and the session goes on. Open the **Multiverse**, select an earlier turn and press **Play from here** to play it differently. See [What the Multiverse is](help:multiverse).

## Good to know

- The Dojo doesn't stop the game at 20. The board stays live.
- The dialog shows once per branch. If you **Undo** below 20 and reach it again, you get the dialog and a new node again.
- Lore isn't capped at 20. The Dojo doesn't check other ways to win or lose, such as an empty deck.

articles.title: Read a card: preview and text mode
articles.summary: See a card large with its full text, in the preview on desktop, in the card drawer on a phone, or in text mode for every card.
articles.body:
Cards on the board are small. The preview shows one large enough to read, with all its abilities.

## See a card large

:::desktop
Point at any card on the board, in a hand, in the discard column, in the draw odds, or in a deck or discard grid. It shows in the preview in the side rail, under the mini multiverse. The last card you pointed at stays there until you point at another.
:::

:::phone
Tap a card in play or in your hand. The card drawer opens with the card's full text and a small picture of it. Step to the next card with ‹ ›, or swipe sideways on the text.

For other cards, such as those in the discard or the other player's hand, tap the card and choose **Preview Card**. The ☰ side panel opens with the card in it.
:::

[Show me](show:card-preview)

## Text mode

Turn on **Text** under **Card display** in Tweaks to show every card as text instead of art. Text mode applies to the board, the hands, the grids and the preview. The text card shows the cost, name, type line, every ability and the stats. The cost sits in a winged hexagon if the card can be inked, or a plain hexagon if not. See [Card size and Art / Text](help:card-display).

## Good to know

- The preview always shows locations as text, so they aren't cropped.
- If a card's art can't load, for example offline, the preview shows its text instead.
- On a tablet, tapping a card in play opens the card drawer. A hand card's menu has **Preview Card**.

articles.title: Look through your deck and reorder it
articles.summary: Open a deck, drag its cards into the order you want, save the order, or shuffle it.
articles.body:
Open a deck to see every card left in it, in draw order, and set up the draws you want to practise.

## Open the deck

:::desktop
Click the magnifier at the top right of the deck, or right-click the deck and choose **Inspect Deck**. Clicking the deck itself draws a card.
:::

:::phone
Tap the ⋮ button on the deck in the player bar, then **Inspect Deck**. Tapping the deck itself draws a card.
:::

[Show me](show:deck)

The grid starts with the top card, which is the next card drawn. This works on both players' decks.

## Reorder it

1. Drag a card onto the place you want it. The card you dropped on moves along.
2. Press **Save Custom Order**. **Cancel** or {key:Esc} leaves the deck as it was.

Saving also adds a node called *Custom deck ordering* to the Multiverse, so you can come back to this order.

## Shuffle it

:::desktop
Click the shuffle button at the bottom right of the deck, or right-click the deck and choose **Shuffle Deck**.
:::

:::phone
Tap ⋮ on the deck, then **Shuffle Deck**.
:::

## Good to know

- The Dojo doesn't stop you from stacking a deck. You're the referee.
- To change which cards are in the deck, see [Swap a card](help:swap-cards).
- **Undo** takes back a shuffle or a saved order.

articles.title: Your discard pile
articles.summary: Read the discard on the board, open it in full, and bring cards back.
articles.body:
Every card that leaves play or is discarded goes to its owner's discard pile. You can read the pile at any time and take cards back out.

## Read the discard

:::desktop
Each half of the board has a **Discard** column. It lists the cards newest first, with cost, strength and lore on the right. Past eight cards, **+N more** shows the rest. Point at a row to see the card in the preview.
:::

:::phone
The discard is the mini card on the player bar. It shows the top card and how many cards are in the pile.
:::

[Show me](show:discard)

## Open it in full

:::desktop
Click the magnifier in the **Discard** header, or right-click the column and choose **Inspect Discard Pile**.
:::

:::phone
Tap the magnifier on the discard's mini card.
:::

The pile opens as a grid of cards, oldest first.

## Bring a card back

:::desktop
Click or right-click a card in the column or the grid. Choose **Play Card to Field**, **Return to Hand**, **Move to Top of Deck** or **Move to Bottom of Deck**. You can also drag a row from the column onto the field, the hand or the deck.
:::

:::phone
Tap a card in the grid, or the top card on the bar, and pick one of the same moves. **Preview Card** shows it large.
:::

The grid stays open, so you can take out several cards.

## Good to know

- The Dojo doesn't check that a card is allowed to come back. You're the referee.
- **Play Card to Field** spends ink when the player has enough ready.

articles.title: Swap a card in your hand or deck
articles.summary: Replace one card, or every copy of it, with any other card to test a different list.

headings.text: Swap a card in your hand

articles.body:
Swap a card for any other card to see how a different list plays, without building a new deck.

## Swap a card in your hand

:::desktop
Right-click the card in your hand and choose **Swap Card**.
:::

:::phone
Tap the card in your hand. In the card drawer, under **More**, press **Swap**.
:::

Type at least two letters of a card's name in **Search Replacement Card**, then click the card you want. It takes the old card's place in the hand at once.

## Replace cards in the deck

1. Open the deck. See [Look through your deck](help:inspect-deck).
2. Right-click a card in the grid and choose **Replace this card**. Choose **Replace all copies** to change every copy of it in the deck.
3. Search and click the new card.
4. Press **Save Custom Order**. Until you do, nothing changes, and **Cancel** throws the replacements away.

:::phone
On a phone, press and hold a card in the deck grid to open its menu. Some phone browsers don't open it, such as Safari on iPhone.
:::

## Good to know

- The search offers every card, not only those in your deck's inks. The Dojo doesn't check that the new card is legal in your deck, or how many copies you have.
- **Replace all copies** only changes the cards in the deck. Copies in your hand, in play or in the discard stay.
- **Undo** takes back a hand swap.
- Swaps change this match only. To change a saved deck, edit it in the Library. See [Your decks](help:decks).

articles.title: Unknown cards and filling them in
articles.summary: An import marks the cards it couldn't see as unknown. Replace them one at a time or all at once.
articles.body:
When you import a Duels.ink game, any card the log or replay never shows becomes an **unknown card**. An unknown card is a card back with no name. You can play on with unknown cards or replace them with real cards.

## Where they show up

- **Decks** hold the cards nobody drew or revealed yet. In the deck grid they show as a card back marked *(Unknown)*.
- **The opponent's hand** holds them when the game never revealed those cards.
- **Cards under a character** are unknown after a boost or shift in a text log.
- **Draw odds** groups them in one **Unknown** row, so you can see how many are left.

## Replace them

1. Open the deck. See [Look through your deck](help:inspect-deck).
2. Right-click an unknown card. **Replace this card** changes that one. **Replace all copies** turns every unknown card in the deck into the card you pick.
3. Press **Save Custom Order**.

You can also swap an unknown card in the other player's hand. Right-click it and choose **Swap Card**. On a phone, tap an unknown card in your hand and press **Swap**. See [Swap a card](help:swap-cards).

## Good to know

- No button fills the unknown cards from a decklist. Replace them by hand, or draw and play with them as they are.
- An unknown card has no cost or stats, so the curve and the odds of named cards leave it out.
- Saving the order adds a node to the Multiverse, so that turn keeps the filled-in deck.

articles.title: Draw odds
articles.summary: The chance to draw each card in your next draws, updated as the game changes.
articles.body:
**Draw odds**, on the right of the board, shows the chance of drawing at least one copy of each card in your next few draws. It follows the active player's deck and updates after every change.

[Show me](show:draw-odds)

## Read the odds

Each row is a card in the player's whole list, wherever its copies are now. Each row has these columns:

- **Left** counts the copies still in the deck.
- The three number columns give the chance, in percent, of drawing at least one copy within the next 1, 2 or 3 draws.

Rows with the most copies left come first. A card with no copies left stays in the list, greyed out with dashes. The number next to the title is the deck size. Point at a row to see the card in the preview.

## Change the draw windows

Click a column's number and type how many draws it should cover, from 1 to 60. The mulligan's odds use the same three windows.

## Hide the pane

Click the arrows at the top right of **Draw odds** to fold it into a thin strip. Click them again to open it.

## Good to know

- The odds assume the deck is in random order. After you stack a deck by hand, they don't know the order you set.
- **Draw odds** groups unknown cards from an import in one **Unknown** row.
- A phone has no draw odds pane. The mulligan shows its own odds. See [Mulligan](help:mulligan).

articles.title: Your decks: new, import, edit
articles.summary: Paste or import a decklist, save it to My decks, edit it, and seat it for a match.

headings.text: Add a deck in the Library

articles.body:
Keep the decks you play in **My decks**, so they're one tap away on the home screen.

## Paste a decklist

Paste a list into the field on the home screen, one card per line, like `4 Tinker Bell - Giant Fairy`. Duels.ink's own export works as it is, with the printing at the end of each line, like `4 Tinker Bell - Giant Fairy (1-193)`. The readout under the field shows the inks, how many of the 60 cards it recognised, and which lines it skipped. Then choose one:

- **Play it as you** or **Play against it** seats the deck for the next match.
- **Save to My decks** keeps it.

[Show me](show:intake)

## Add a deck in the Library

Open **Library**, then **Decks**. There are three ways to add a deck:

- **New deck.** Type a name, paste the list, add notes if you like, and press **Save deck**.
- **Import .txt.** Pick a text file with a decklist. It opens in the same form to check and save.
- **From a replay.** Pick a Duels.ink replay file in .json, .replay or .replay.gz format. The form fills with your exact 60 from that game.

[Show me](show:deck-new)

## Edit, seat or delete

Each deck has **You** and **Opponent** to seat it. Its **⋯** menu has **Edit**, **Share a link** and **Delete…**. Saving an edit updates any seat that holds that deck.

## Good to know

- The Dojo doesn't check deck rules. A list that isn't 60 cards plays with the cards it has, and the seat's count turns amber.
- If the Dojo recognises no card, the deck is 60 random cards.
- My decks live in this browser. Signing in also keeps them in your account. See [The Library](help:library).

articles.title: Built-in decks and demos
articles.summary: Ready-made decks for each set and example sessions to explore, all without signing in.
articles.body:
The Dojo comes with a few decks and example games, so you can start without a list of your own.

## Play a built-in deck

On the home screen, under **On the table**, pick a deck under **Default decks**. It goes to the first open seat, **You** first and then **Opponent**. Press **Start match**. The heading folds the default decks away, and the Dojo remembers that. Searching or picking an ink shows them again.

[Show me](show:deck-chips)

The Library's **Decks** tab lists them on the **Built in** shelf, grouped by set, with **You** and **Opponent** to seat them. To make your own version, open its **⋯** menu and choose **Copy to my decks and edit**.

## Explore a demo

Under **Pick up again**, the demos are marked *Demo · opens as your own copy*. Press **Explore** to open one. A demo is a full game with its Multiverse, which you can step through and play from any turn.

[Show me](show:recent)

## Good to know

- A demo opens as a copy in your sessions. Change the copy as much as you like. The demo itself stays the same.
- Built-in decks are the same for everyone, and you can't edit them in place.
- **A decklist**, under the paste field, puts a built-in list in the field to try.
- An empty seat plays 60 random cards.

articles.title: What the Multiverse is
articles.summary: Every saved turn is a node in a tree. Jump to any of them and play a different line from there.
articles.body:
The Multiverse keeps every turn you've saved, so you can go back to any of them and play it another way.

Each saved board is a **node**. Nodes link up turn by turn into a line, which is the game as you played it. Go back to an earlier node and play on from it, and the new turns grow a second line from that point. That second line is a branch. All the lines together make a tree, and that tree is the Multiverse. Use it to answer a question like "what if I had challenged instead of quested on turn 6?". Play both lines and compare them.

## Open the Multiverse

:::desktop
Click **Multiverse** in the top bar, or press {key:M}. Press {key:M}, {key:Esc} or the ✕ to go back to the board.
:::

:::phone
Tap the branch icon in the top bar. Tap ✕ to go back to the board.
:::

[Show me](show:multiverse)

## What you see

- **The canvas** draws the tree, with the earliest turns on the left. The path from the start to the node you're on is highlighted, and the other lines are grey.
- **The panel** sits beside the canvas, or under it on a phone. It shows the node you select, with **Play from here**, and holds **Save current unfinished turn**. With the rules engine on, **What-if** in the header opens [What-if](help:what-if) at the top of the panel.

[Show me](show:tree-panel)

## Good to know

- Nodes come from three places. [Auto-save](help:auto-save) adds one at the start of each turn, [saving the turn you're in](help:save-unfinished-turn) adds one, and imported Duels.ink games add theirs. When a player reaches 20 lore, the Dojo also saves a **Game Over** node that closes the branch.
- Selecting a node only shows it. Your board changes when you press **Play from here**.
- Jumping never loses the board you leave. See ["Left here" snapshots](help:left-here).
- The tree is part of the session, and the Dojo saves it with the session. **Export** in the Multiverse header writes the session to a file, tree included.

articles.title: Every turn is saved
articles.summary: With auto-save on, every turn gets a node in the Multiverse with the board it starts from and what was done in it.
articles.body:
With **Auto-save every turn** on, the Dojo gives every turn a node in the Multiverse. It saves the whole game turn by turn without you doing anything.

## Turn auto-save on or off

:::desktop
The **Auto-save every turn** switch sits at the foot of the side rail, above **Quest** and **End turn**.

[Show me](show:auto-save)
:::

:::phone
Open the ☰ menu. The **Auto-save every turn** switch is near the bottom, above **Quest** and **End turn**.

[Show me](show:menu)
:::

## What an auto-save keeps

When a turn starts, after the player has readied and drawn, the Dojo saves the board as a node. Its name gives the turn and the player. **Turn 5 - Player 2 Active** holds the board at the start of Player 2's turn 5. When that turn ends, the same node gets these:

- the note written for that turn. See [Turn notes](help:turn-notes).
- a **Turn recap** of what was drawn, inked, played, shifted, discarded, quested, challenged and banished that turn.
- the cards behind the recap, in sections such as **Played**, **Inked** and **Drawn**.

So a node is one turn, with the board it starts from and what was done in it. Load it to play that turn again. The new node hangs off the node you were on, so the tree follows the line you're playing.

## Good to know

- With the switch off, ending a turn saves nothing. Save by hand with [Save current unfinished turn](help:save-unfinished-turn).
- The switch is on each time you open the Dojo. Turning it off lasts until you reload.
- Each player's turn 1 node holds the dealt hand, before the mulligan. Load it to mulligan again or build a different opening hand.
- If you play a turn again from its node and end it, the new line gets a node of its own beside the old one. The old node keeps its note and recap. See [Branching](help:branches).
- When a player reaches 20 lore, the Dojo saves a **Game Over** node even with auto-save off.

articles.title: Save the turn you're in
articles.summary: Save the board mid-turn as a node, with a name and a note.
articles.body:
Save the board as it is now, in the middle of a turn, as a node you can come back to. Save before a risky challenge, for example, or at a moment you want to study later.

## Save current unfinished turn

:::desktop
Press {key:T} on the board, or open the Multiverse and click **Save current unfinished turn** at the top of the panel.
:::

:::phone
Open the Multiverse and tap **Save current unfinished turn** at the top of the panel, under the canvas.
:::

[Show me](show:save-turn)

The button opens a short form:

1. **Name** starts as **Turn 7 - Player 1 (unfinished)**. Change it to say what the node is for.
2. **Note** starts with your turn note and a recap of what you've drawn, inked and played so far this turn. Edit it as you like. Markdown works.
3. **This node keeps** shows the cards the node will record, by section.
4. Press **Save node**. **Cancel** closes the form without saving.

:::desktop
In the **Name** field, {key:Enter} saves. {key:Esc} closes the form.
:::

## Good to know

- Your board doesn't change, so carry on playing. The new node hangs off the node you were on and becomes the one you're on, so the next auto-save hangs off it.
- You can rename the node or change its note later in [the panel](help:multiverse-panel).
- **Save as copy** in the top bar does something else. It copies the whole session.

articles.title: Reading a node
articles.summary: What a node shows, including whose turn it is, the lore, the note, the turn recap and the cards played.
articles.body:
A node is one saved board. In the cards view each node is a small card. This article explains how to read it. A phone opens the Multiverse on the plot, so tap **Plot** in the header for the cards. See [Cards and plot](help:multiverse-views).

## What's on a node

- **Tone.** A light card is Player 1's turn, and a dark card is Player 2's. The deck icon shows the same.
- **Name.** An auto-save is named like **Turn 16 - Player 2 Active**, which is the board at the start of that player's turn. The name of a turn you saved yourself ends in **(unfinished)**.
- **Subline.** It gives the turn, the lore, like **P1: 10 - P2: 11**, and the time the node was saved.
- **Note.** A dark box holds the turn's note and its **Turn recap** of what was drawn, inked and played. Click it to edit it in the panel.
- **Played.** It lists the cards played that turn.
- **The bin.** It deletes the node, and **Undo** brings it back.

## Which node is which

- **The node you're on** is the one your board came from. It has a coloured border and foot, and the path to it is highlighted. The panel calls it **· you are here**.
- **The selected node** is the one the panel shows. It has four corner marks around it.
- **A "Left here" snapshot** has a dashed outline and a dashed line to its node. See ["Left here" snapshots](help:left-here).
- **A won branch** ends in a **Game Over** node with a trophy, a plate with the winner's lore and **Branch closed**, and a short bar after it.

## Every card section

Select a node to see all its card sections in the panel. They are **Played**, **Inked**, **Drawn**, **Discarded**, **Banished**, **Quested** and **Starting hand**. In **Starting hand**, cards that left the hand that turn are crossed out. To show every section inside every node, turn on **Show in nodes** under **Turn recap** in the panel.

[Show me](show:tree-canvas)

## Good to know

- You can change the name and the note. See [The panel](help:multiverse-panel).
- On an auto-save, **Turn recap** lists what was done in that node's turn. A turn still being played has no recap yet.

articles.title: The panel: select, play from here, rename, notes, delete
articles.summary: Select a node to read it in the panel, play from it, rename it, edit its note or delete it.
articles.body:
The panel shows the node you select. Read it there first, then play from it, rename it, change its note or delete it.

## Select a node

:::desktop
Click a node, or a dot in the plot. The arrow keys move the selection. See [Moving around](help:multiverse-navigate).
:::

:::phone
Tap a node or a dot, or move the cursor with the thumb keys. The panel is under the canvas, so scroll down to read all of it.
:::

Selecting doesn't change your board. The panel shows these parts:

- **Selected**, with **· you are here** on the node you're on.
- The name, the turn, the lore and the time.
- The note.
- **Lore race · this line**, which draws both players' lore turn by turn from turn 1 to this node. P1 is solid, P2 is dashed, and the line at 20 is the winning score.
- The **Turn recap** as cards.

[Show me](show:selected-node)

## Play from here

Press **Play from here**. The board becomes that node's board and the Multiverse closes.

:::desktop
You can also double-click the node, or press {key:Enter}.
:::

If the board you left wasn't saved, the Dojo keeps it as a ["Left here" snapshot](help:left-here).

## Rename a node

Click its name in the panel, type, and press {key:Enter} or click away. {key:Esc} cancels.

## Edit the note

Click the note, or **Add a note…** when it's empty. You can edit the whole text, turn recap included, and Markdown works. Click away to save. {key:Esc} cancels.

:::desktop
{key:Ctrl+Enter} also saves. Clicking a note on a node opens it here.
:::

## Delete a node

Press the bin, in the panel or on the node. Its later turns stay, and move up to hang off the node before it. The toast offers **Undo**.

## Good to know

:::desktop
The panel docks on the right. The columns button in the Multiverse header moves it to the left and back, and the Dojo remembers the side. [Show me](show:tree-dock)
:::

- A "Left here" snapshot has **Keep as node** instead of a name and note to edit.

articles.title: Branching: try another line
articles.summary: Play from an earlier node and do something different. The new turns grow a new branch.
articles.body:
To try another line, go back to an earlier node and play on from it. The new turns grow a new branch, and the line you played before stays as it was.

## Try another line

1. Open the Multiverse and select the node to go back to. An auto-save named **Turn 6 - Player 1 Active** is the board at the start of Player 1's turn 6, so pick it to replay that turn.
2. Press **Play from here**. You're back on the board, at that point in the game.
3. Play the turn differently and end it. With auto-save on, your new line gets a node of its own beside the one you played from. It has the same board and your new recap, and the next turn hangs off it. That is a branch. On turn 1 this is where you mulligan again or build a different hand.
4. Keep playing. Every turn you end adds to the new line.

[Show me](show:tree-canvas)

## Compare the lines

The path to the node you're on is highlighted, and the other lines are grey. Select nodes on each line and compare their **Lore race** and **Turn recap** in the panel. The plot shows the whole game at once. See [Cards and plot](help:multiverse-views).

## Good to know

- Branching never changes or deletes the nodes you already have.
- If the board you leave wasn't saved, the Dojo keeps it as a ["Left here" snapshot](help:left-here).
- **Undo** doesn't reach across a jump. Its history starts fresh from the node you play from.
- When a player reaches 20 lore, a **Game Over** node closes the branch, and the Dojo offers **View Multiverse** or **Stay Here**. You can still go back and play a branch where the other player wins.

articles.title: "Left here" snapshots
articles.summary: When you jump away from an unsaved board, the Dojo keeps it as a dashed "Left here" snapshot.

headings.text: When the Dojo keeps a snapshot

articles.body:
When you jump to another node from a board you haven't saved, the Dojo first keeps that board as a "Left here" snapshot. A jump never loses your work.

## When the Dojo keeps a snapshot

Every jump checks the board you're leaving. A jump is **Play from here**, or on desktop a double-click, {key:Enter} or a click in the mini multiverse. If the board has changed since it was loaded or saved, the Dojo keeps it as a snapshot. If the board matches a node or snapshot that's still in the tree, the Dojo adds nothing.

## Find a snapshot

![A node, and the dashed "Left here" snapshot hanging off it on a dashed line](img/left-here-{theme}.webp)

A snapshot hangs off the node you were last on, on a dashed line:

- In the cards view, it's a dashed card titled **Left here** with the time, like **Left here · 14:32**.
- In the plot, it's a dashed ring.
- In the mini multiverse, it's a dashed hollow dot.

## Use a snapshot

Select it. The panel says **Where you jumped from** and offers these:

- **Play from here** loads that board again.
- **Keep as node** turns it into a real node where it hangs, named like **Turn 9 - Player 1 (kept 14:32)**. Then you can rename it and write a note.
- The bin discards it. The toast offers **Undo**.

[Show me](show:tree-canvas)

## Good to know

- The Dojo keeps only the last five snapshots. A sixth pushes out the oldest, so keep the ones that matter as nodes.
- A snapshot isn't a node until you keep it. You can't rename it, and it has no note.

articles.title: Cards and plot
articles.summary: Switch between full node cards and the plot, where every saved turn is a dot.
articles.body:
The Multiverse draws the tree in two views. The cards view shows full nodes you can read. The plot shows every saved turn as a dot, so you can see a whole game at once.

## Switch between cards and plot

:::desktop
Click **Plot** in the Multiverse header. It stays dark while the plot is on. Click it again for the cards. The Dojo remembers your choice.
:::

:::phone
Tap **Plot** in the Multiverse header, left of ✕, to switch to the cards while the Multiverse is open. Its icon is a grid of dots. A phone always opens the Multiverse on the plot, because the cards are too wide for the screen.
:::

[Show me](show:plot-toggle)

## Read the plot

- Each saved turn is a dot in its deck's two inks. Player 1's dots are solid and Player 2's are striped. The turn number sits under each dot.
- A ruler along the top gives each column's turn and player, **P1** or **P2**.
- Lines run from each turn to the next. The path to the node you're on is highlighted. "Left here" snapshots hang on dashed lines.
- **You are here** is a ring around the dot your board came from.
- **Cursor** is a crosshair on the selected dot. Its tag gives the turn, player and lore, like **T12 · P1 · 7–6**.
- **20 lore · branch closed** marks a won branch. It ends in a square dot and a bar, with the winner's lore and name.
- **Left here** is a dashed ring.

A key names all of these. It runs along the foot of the canvas on desktop and along its top on a phone.

[Show me](show:tree-legend)

## Good to know

- Click or tap a dot to select it, as with a card. The panel shows it.
- On desktop the plot opens fitted to the whole game. A phone opens it close up, on the cursor. The zoom out thumb key shows the whole game. See [Moving around](help:multiverse-navigate).
- The cards show more of each turn, and the plot shows the shape of the game.

articles.title: Moving around: keys, thumb keys, zoom
articles.summary: Pan, zoom, and step through turns and lines with the arrow keys or the thumb keys.
articles.body:
Move around the Multiverse canvas, and step the selection through turns and lines to find the one you want. Nothing loads until you press **Play from here**.

## Pan and zoom

:::desktop
Drag the canvas to pan. Scroll to zoom in or out at the pointer. **Reset zoom** is the button left of ✕. In the plot it fits the whole game. In the cards it goes back to full size at the start of the tree.

[Show me](show:tree-zoom-reset)
:::

:::phone
Drag with one finger to pan, and {gesture:pinch} to zoom.
:::

## Arrow keys

:::desktop
The arrow keys move the selection, and the canvas follows it:

- {key:←} selects the turn before.
- {key:→} selects the turn after. If the line branches there, it picks the oldest branch.
- {key:↑} and {key:↓} select the next branch up or down from the same node.
- {key:Enter} plays from the selected node.
:::

## Thumb keys

:::phone
Six keys sit at the canvas's foot. They move the cursor, and the panel under the canvas shows the turn it's on.

- **◀** goes to the turn before. **▶** goes to the turn after, back the way you came if you can, or else along the line you're on.
- **▲** and **▼** go to the nearest turn on another line above or below, near the same point in the game.
- **◎** goes back to the node you're on.
- **Zoom out**, the magnifier, fits the whole game. Press it again, or step, to come back in close. Only the plot has it.

Hold an arrow to keep stepping. A key that can't go anywhere is hollow.

[Show me](show:tree-keys)
:::

## Good to know

- Opening the Multiverse selects the node you're on, or the newest node, and centres on it.
- On desktop, the [mini multiverse](help:mini-multiverse) in the side rail steps through the tree and loads each turn at once.

articles.title: The mini multiverse
articles.summary: The small map beside the board. Click a dot to jump, step through a line, and find branch points.
articles.body:
The mini multiverse is a small map of the whole tree in the side rail, under the players. Jump to any turn with one click, or step through a line, without opening the full Multiverse.

![The mini multiverse, with the line you're on in orange, other lines in grey, and the step keys under the map](img/mini-multiverse-{theme}.webp)

## Read the map

- Each dot is a saved turn, and each row is a line. A branch takes the nearest free row.
- The line you're on is highlighted, with filled dots. If you stepped back along the line, the turns ahead of you on it are dashed rings.
- The node you're on has a ring. The ring turns dashed once the board has changed since that node.
- "Left here" snapshots are dashed hollow dots. A won branch ends in a square dot and a bar.
- The head gives the turn, player and lore, like **T14 · P2 · 8–8**. It shows the node you're on, or the dot under the pointer. That dot's name shows at the foot.
- **Edited · kept if you jump** at the foot means your board has changed since its node.

[Show me](show:mini-multiverse)

## Jump to a turn

Click a dot and the board becomes that turn at once, with no **Play from here**. Drag or scroll the map to pan. The button in the head opens the full Multiverse.

## Step through a line

The keys under the map load the turn they step to:

- **⏮** goes back to the last branch point behind you, or to the start.
- **◀** goes to the turn before. **▶** goes to the next turn on the line.
- **⏭** goes on to the next branch point ahead, or to the end of the line.
- **↑** and **↓** go to the nearest turn on the line above or below.

Click the map first, and {key:←} {key:→} {key:↑} {key:↓}, {key:Home} and {key:End} do the same.

[Show me](show:mini-multiverse-keys)

## Lore race

Under the map, **Lore race** draws both players' lore turn by turn along the line you're on, from turn 1. P1 is the solid line and P2 the dashed one. The dashed line at the top is 20, the winning score. The orange numbers at the right are the lore at the node you're on, which a thin orange line marks. Turns ahead of you on the line show faint. The chart follows every jump and step.

[Show me](show:lore-race)

## Good to know

- Stepping back keeps the rest of the line ahead of you, so **▶** retraces it.
- On a board you've changed since its node, **◀** reloads that node and **▶** goes on to the next turn.
- If you leave a board unsaved, the Dojo keeps it as a ["Left here" snapshot](help:left-here).
- Phones don't show the map or the lore race. Use the [thumb keys](help:multiverse-navigate) in the Multiverse instead.

articles.title: Study a Duels.ink game
articles.summary: Paste or drop a Duels.ink log or replay and the Dojo rebuilds the game turn by turn as a Multiverse.
articles.body:
Bring a game you played on Duels.ink into the Dojo to look at it turn by turn and try other lines from any point.

## Bring in a game

1. Open the home screen.
2. Paste the game's text log into the field, or press **Choose a file** for a replay file. You can also drop a file anywhere on the page.
3. The readout says what it found. It shows a **Duels.ink log** with its number of turns, or a **Duels.ink replay** with the players' names.
4. Press **Study this game**.

[Show me](show:readout)

To try it without a game of your own, press **A Duels.ink log** under the field to load an example.

## What you get

- A new session named after the date and the players or their inks, with *(Duels.ink)* at the end.
- One Multiverse node per turn. Its note holds the turn's moves, and its card sections hold the cards played, inked, drawn and so on.
- The board at the end of the game.

Open **Multiverse**, pick a turn and press **Play from here** to load it, then play it differently. See [The Multiverse](help:multiverse).

## Good to know

- A replay file gives the most exact rebuild, and a text log also works. Compare them in [Import a text log](help:import-log) and [Import a replay file](help:import-replay).
- Some cards stay unknown. See [What an import knows and doesn't](help:hidden-information).
- The Dojo can't fetch games from Duels.ink by itself. Copy or download the game there first.

articles.title: Import a text log
articles.summary: Copy the match log from Duels.ink and paste it into the home screen or the Multiverse's Log tool.
articles.body:
A Duels.ink text log lists every move of a game. Paste it into the Dojo and every turn becomes a node in the Multiverse.

## From the home screen

1. Copy the whole log from Duels.ink.
2. Paste it into the field on the home screen. If you paste anywhere else on the page, the log still lands in the field.
3. Check that the readout shows **Duels.ink log** and *A N-turn game*.
4. Press **Study this game**.

[Show me](show:intake)

A log saved as a .txt or .md file also works. Press **Choose a file**.

## From the Multiverse

Open **Multiverse** and press **Log** in its header. Paste the log into **Import Duels.ink Log**, or choose a file. When the message under it says the log is valid, press **Import**. The game opens as a new session, and the one you were in stays in your Library.

[Show me](show:tree-log)

## Which logs work

Both of Duels.ink's formats work. The newer one says *You* and *Opponent*, and the older one says *Player 1* and *Player 2*. The log needs its `--- Turn 1 ---` lines. Without the starting hand lines it still imports, with a warning that the Dojo can place fewer cards.

## Good to know

- In the Dojo, the log's owner, *You*, is Player 1.
- The newer log hides the opponent's hand and draws. See [What an import knows and doesn't](help:hidden-information).
