- Cards the log never names come in as unknown cards. See [Unknown cards](help:unknown-cards).

articles.title: Import a replay file
articles.summary: Drop the replay file Duels.ink gives you, in .json, .replay or .replay.gz format, for the most exact rebuild.
articles.body:
A Duels.ink replay file records the game exactly. It's the best way to bring a game in, because your own deck comes through card for card, in order.

## Import it

1. Download the replay from Duels.ink. It usually ends in **.replay.gz**. You don't need to unzip it.
2. On the home screen, press **Choose a file** and pick it, or drop the file anywhere on the page.
3. The readout shows **Duels.ink replay**, the two players and the number of turns.
4. Press **Study this game**.

[Show me](show:intake-file)

You can also open **Multiverse**, press **Log**, choose the file and press **Import**.

## Play your deck from it

The readout's **Play my deck from it** seats the deck you played as **You**, ready for a new match. To keep that deck, use **From a replay** in the Library's **Decks** tab. See [Your decks](help:decks).

## Good to know

- The players keep their Duels.ink names and seats. If you were the second player, you're Player 2.
- Your deck is exact, in its real order. The opponent's hidden cards stay unknown until they show them. See [What an import knows and doesn't](help:hidden-information).
- Only replay files carry a decklist. A text log can't give you **Play my deck from it**.

articles.title: What an import knows and doesn't
articles.summary: A replay gives your own deck exactly. The opponent's hidden cards stay unknown until they reveal them.
articles.body:
An import can only show what the game showed. Any card nobody saw comes in as an [unknown card](help:unknown-cards).

## From a replay file

- **Your deck** is exact. It has every card, in the order you'd have drawn it.
- **The opponent's hand and deck** are hidden. The Dojo puts the cards they play, ink or show later back into their hand and deck in the earlier turns. The soonest cards go in the hand and the rest go in the deck. Cards they never show stay unknown.

## From a text log

- **Your deck** has the cards you go on to draw on top, in order. The log never names the rest of the deck, so it's unknown.
- **The opponent's** opening hand and draws are hidden in the newer *You / Opponent* log. As with a replay, the Dojo fills in cards they reveal later, and the rest stay unknown.
- The older *Player 1 / Player 2* log shows both hands, so both sides work like your own.
- The log doesn't name a card put face down into the inkwell or under a character.

## Good to know

- The place of the opponent's hidden cards, in the hand or the deck, is the Dojo's best guess.
- A text log can miss a step that a replay has, such as an ability that exerts a character without naming it.
- Fix anything you know better. You can [swap cards](help:swap-cards) in a hand, or replace them in the deck.

articles.title: Sessions save themselves
articles.summary: Every match is a session. The Dojo keeps it on this device as you play and lists it under Pick up again.
articles.body:
A session is one match with its whole Multiverse. The Dojo keeps every session on this device as you play, so you never lose a match by closing the tab.

## What makes a session

A new session starts when you do one of these:

- press **Start match** on the home screen.
- open a saved session file.
- study a Duels.ink log or replay.
- open a demo, which opens as your own copy.

The Dojo names it from the date and the decks, like *Oct 13 · Steelsong Tempo vs Ruby/Sapphire*. It uses a deck's name, or its inks when the deck has no name. You can rename it. See [Save, save as copy, rename](help:save-and-rename).

## Saving happens by itself

The Dojo saves every change to this device about a second after you make it, and again when you switch tabs or close the page. You don't have to press **Save**. Leaving to the home screen also keeps the match.

## Pick up again

The home screen's **Pick up again** box lists **Your sessions** first. The last session comes first with **Resume**, then your most recent ones. The **Demos** come after them with **Explore**. The match on the board says **Back to it**. **All sessions** opens the [Library](help:library) with every session you have.

**Find a session or a card in it** searches all your sessions and the demos, by title or by a card in either deck. The search allows typos and missing letters, so `lvthn` finds The Leviathan. A row found by a card names that card. The ink buttons narrow the list. One ink shows what uses it, and two show that exact pair. The arrow on **Demos** folds them away, and they stay folded next time.

[Show me](show:recent)

## Good to know

- Sessions live in this browser on this device. Clearing the site's data or closing a private window deletes them, and another browser or device doesn't have them. Export a file to keep a backup, or [sign in](help:account) to keep them in an account. See [Where your things are kept](help:storage).
- **Auto-save every turn** does something else. It saves a node in the [Multiverse](help:auto-save) at each turn. The switch is in the side rail, or the ☰ menu on a phone.
- If the Dojo can't save to this device, it tells you once with "Couldn't save to this device. Export the session to keep it."

articles.title: Save, save as copy, rename
articles.summary: Name the session, save it now, or save a copy to try something without changing the original.
articles.body:
Give the match on the board a name, save it at once, or split off a copy to try a different idea.

## Rename the session

:::desktop
Click the session title at the top left of the top bar, type a new name and press {key:Enter}. {key:Esc} puts the old name back.

[Show me](show:session-title)
:::

:::phone
The top bar has no title on a phone. Tap **⋯** and choose **Leave to the dojo**. The match stays saved. Open **Library**, then open the session's **⋯** and choose **Rename**.
:::

You can rename any session the same way from the [Library](help:library). Open its **⋯** and choose **Rename**.

## Save now

The Dojo already saves as you play. See [Sessions save themselves](help:sessions). **Save** writes the session at once and tells you so. If you're signed in, it also saves the session to your account. See [What goes to your account](help:account-sync).

:::desktop
Press the floppy-disk button next to the title.

[Show me](show:save)
:::

:::phone
Tap **⋯** in the top bar, then **Save**.
:::

## Save as copy

Use it before trying a risky line. The copy carries on, and the original stays as it was.

:::desktop
Press the copy button next to **Save**.
:::

:::phone
Tap **⋯**, then **Save as copy**.
:::

Name the copy and press **Save copy**. The copy becomes the session on the board. The original keeps everything up to that moment.

## Good to know

- A new copy is only on this device. If you're signed in, press **Save** to put it in your account too.
- To copy a session without opening it, open its **⋯** in the Library and choose **Duplicate**.
- While you view someone's shared link, **Save** saves your own copy of it. See [Open a link someone sent you](help:open-a-shared-link).

articles.title: The Library: sessions, decks, links
articles.summary: Everything you keep, on shelves by where it lives. The shelves are this device, your account, built in and public links.

headings.text: Find a session or a deck

articles.body:
The Library holds every session and deck you keep, sorted onto shelves by where each one lives.

## Open the Library

On the home screen, press **Library** at the top, or **All sessions** in **Pick up again**. The figures on the button count your sessions on this device and, when you're signed in, in your account. {key:Esc} or **×** closes it.

[Show me](show:library-button)

From a match, leave to the home screen first. See [The screen at a glance](help:screen-at-a-glance).

## The tabs

- **Sessions** lists every match you've kept. **Open** loads one, and the match on the board shows **Back to it** instead. Its **⋯** menu has **Rename**, **Share a link**, **Duplicate**, **Export file (.dojo.json.gz)** and **Delete…**. **Import file** adds a session file. See [Export and import session files](help:files).
- **Decks** lists your decks and the **Built in** ones. **You** and **Opponent** seat a deck for the next match. **New deck**, **Import .txt** and **From a replay** add one. See [Your decks](help:decks).
- **Links** lists the share links you made, under **Public links**. See [Share a deck or a session](help:share-links).

## Find a session or a deck

**Sessions** has **Find a session or a card in it** at the top, and **Decks** has **Find a deck or a card in one**. Type a name or a card. The search allows typos and missing letters, so `lvthn` finds The Leviathan. A row found by a card names that card. The ink buttons narrow the list. One ink shows what uses it, and two show that exact pair. A session matches when either of its decks does. The Dojo reads a session's cards the first time you search. While you search, only the shelves with matches show.

[Show me](show:lib-decks-find)

## The shelves

When you're signed out, your sessions and decks sit on **On this device**, with an empty **Your account** shelf that offers **Sign in**. When you're signed in, they sort into **In your account + this device**, **Only on this device** and **Only in your account**. Each shelf says in one line what that means.

The **Built in** shelf folds away with the arrow on its heading, and stays folded next time. Searching shows it again.

A row adds a note only when it's out of step, like **Changed here since your last Save**. See [What goes to your account](help:account-sync).

:::phone
Each row's buttons sit at the foot of its card.
:::

## Good to know

- You can't undo **Delete…** on a session or deck. Export a session first if you might want it back.
- **On this device** means this browser only. Clearing its site data deletes everything on that shelf. See [Where your things are kept](help:storage).

articles.title: Export and import session files
articles.summary: Save a session as a file to back it up or send it, and open a session file.
articles.body:
A session file holds a whole match, with the board, every Multiverse node, the notes and the log. Export one to keep a backup outside this browser, or to send it to someone by hand.

## Export a session

- **The match on the board.** Open the **Multiverse** and press **Export** at the top.
- **Any session.** In the Library, open the session's **⋯** and choose **Export file (.dojo.json.gz)**.

:::phone
In the Multiverse the file tools show only their icons. **Export** is the file with an arrow pointing out.
:::

[Show me](show:tree-export)

The file is named after the session, like `T8 study.dojo.json.gz`. The Dojo leaves out characters a file name can't hold, such as `/`. The file is compressed, so even a big Multiverse stays small. A browser that can't compress saves a plain `.dojo.json` instead.

## Open a session file

Any of these works:

- On the home screen, press **Choose a file**, or drop the file anywhere on the page. The Dojo reads it and shows **Saved session**. Press **Open it**.
- In the Library's **Sessions** tab, press **Import file**.
- In the Multiverse, press **Import**.

[Show me](show:intake-file)

The Dojo reads `.dojo.json.gz`, `.dojo.json` and older `.json` session files.

## Good to know

- Opening a file always adds a new session to your library and puts it on the board. Opening the same file twice gives you two sessions.
- Your files never go anywhere unless you send them. To send a match without a file, make a [share link](help:share-links).
- A file made by a newer Dojo asks you to reload the page to update first.

articles.title: Share a deck or a session
articles.summary: Make a short link to a deck or a whole multiverse. Anyone can open it without an account.

headings.text: Share the match on the board

articles.body:
A share link sends a deck, or a whole match with its Multiverse, to anyone. They open it in their browser, and neither of you needs an account.

## Share the match on the board

:::desktop
Press the share button next to **Save** in the top bar.

[Show me](show:share)
:::

:::phone
Tap **⋯** in the top bar, then **Share link**.
:::

## Share from the Library

- **A session.** In **Sessions**, open its **⋯** and choose **Share a link**.
- **A deck.** In **Decks**, open its **⋯** and choose **Share a link**. You can share built-in decks too.

## Copy the link

When it's ready, the **Link ready** box shows a short link like `practicedojo.win/app/?s=k3J9xQ2mPa`. Press **Copy link**, then paste it wherever you like.

## See and delete your links

The Library's **Links** tab lists your links under **Public links**. Press **Copy link** to copy one again. Its **⋯** has **Open in a new tab** and **Delete link**. A deleted link stops working for everyone, and opens as "This share is no longer available".

[Show me](show:lib-links)

## Good to know

- A link is a snapshot. Later changes aren't in it, so share again to send a newer version.
- Anyone who has the link can open it. A session link carries everything in the session, including your notes.
- Making a link needs a connection. The first time, the Dojo gives this browser its own sharing identity without a sign-in screen.
- When you're signed out, the **Links** tab lists the links made from this browser. Clearing its site data loses that list, but the links keep working. When you're signed in, links belong to your account. Links this browser made before you signed in move to your account, unless that Discord or Google account was already a Dojo account.
- The limits are 20 links a day, 100 in all, and sessions up to 10 MB compressed. See [Share link limits](help:share-limits).

articles.title: Open a link someone sent you
articles.summary: A shared session opens on the board, unsaved until you save a copy. A shared deck lands on the home screen.
articles.body:
Open the link in your browser. You don't need an account, and the Dojo saves nothing until you choose to keep it.

## A shared session

The match opens on the board with a bar at the top. The bar shows **Shared**, the title, **not saved yet** and **Save a copy**.

[Show me](show:shared-banner)

Look around, play on and open the Multiverse. While the bar shows, nothing goes into your library. To keep the match, press **Save a copy**. **Save** in the top bar does the same. The match becomes your own session on this device, under the same title, and the Dojo saves it from then on like any other.

If you open something else instead, or reload the page, your changes to the shared match are gone. A reload opens the link again from the start.

## A shared deck

The Dojo opens the home screen with the deck in the paste field, marked **Shared deck** with its name. Press **Play it as you** or **Play against it** to seat it, or **Save to My decks** to keep it.

[Show me](show:intake)

## If it doesn't open

- **Link not recognised** means part of the link is missing. Ask for it again, or check that you copied all of it.
- **This share is no longer available** means the person who shared it deleted it.
- **Couldn't open the link** means the Dojo couldn't reach the sharing service. Check your connection and try again.

## Good to know

- Your copy is yours. Changing it never changes the link or the sharer's session.
- A shared link is a snapshot of the moment it was made. If the sharer keeps playing, ask for a new link.

articles.title: Why sign in (and why you don't have to)
articles.summary: Everything works signed out. Signing in keeps your decks and sessions on every device.
articles.body:
An account is optional. It keeps your decks and sessions outside this browser, so they're on every device you sign in on.

## Signed out, everything works

Without an account you can play, use the Multiverse, study Duels.ink games, keep decks and sessions in the Library, export files, and make and open share links. When you're signed out, nothing about accounts loads. The Dojo only goes online to load itself and the cards, and when you make or open a share link.

Without an account, your library lives only in this browser on this device. Clearing the site's data, or closing a private window, deletes it, and another browser or device doesn't have it. Export files to keep a backup. See [Where your things are kept](help:storage).

## What signing in adds

- **Decks follow you.** A deck you save goes to your account by itself and shows up on your other devices.
- **Sessions go up when you press Save.** **Save** puts the match in your account. On another device, open it from the Library.
- **The Library shows where things are.** Its shelves sort everything by place, either in your account and on this device, only on this device, or only in your account.
- **Your share links belong to your account.**

The details are in [What goes to your account](help:account-sync).

## Good to know

- You sign in with Discord or Google. See [Sign in and out](help:sign-in).
- An account holds up to 50 sessions and 200 decks. Sessions that don't fit can stay on this device.
- Your Tweaks, such as the theme and card size, stay with this browser. They don't go to your account.
- Signing in needs a connection. If the Dojo can't reach the account, everything on this device still works.

articles.title: Sign in and out
articles.summary: Sign in with Discord or Google, choose what to bring from this device, and sign out safely on a shared computer.
articles.body:
Sign in to keep your decks and sessions in an account. An account is optional. See [Why sign in](help:account).

## Sign in

1. On the home screen, press **Sign in** at the top. The Library's **Your account** shelf also has a **Sign in** button.
2. Choose **Continue with Discord** or **Continue with Google**.
3. Approve the Dojo on Discord's or Google's page. You come back to the Dojo, signed in, and the button shows your name.

[Show me](show:account-button)

The Dojo gets your name, picture and email from Discord or Google. It never sees your password.

## Bring what's on this device

The first time you sign in on a device that already has decks or sessions, the Dojo asks whether to save them to your account:

- **All** saves every one.
- **Choose…** opens the Library. **Save to account** in a row's **⋯** saves one row. **Save all N to account** on the **Only on this device** shelf saves the whole shelf.
- **Not now** leaves them on this device only. You can still save them from the Library later.

Whichever you choose, they also stay on this device.

## Your account

Press your name on the home screen to see who you're signed in as and how much of your account you use. An account holds up to 50 sessions and 200 decks.

## Sign out

Press your name, then **Sign out**. The Dojo asks what to do with the copies of your account's decks and sessions on this device:

- **Keep on this device** leaves them here, for you or anyone using this browser.
- **Remove from this device** is for a shared computer. The Dojo first saves to your account any changes it doesn't have yet. Anything it can't save stays on this device, and the Dojo tells you how many.

Sessions and decks that were never in an account stay on the device in both cases.

## Good to know

- Share links you made from this browser before signing in move to your account. If your Discord or Google account was already a Dojo account, the Dojo offers to sign in to it instead, and those links stay with this browser.

articles.title: What goes to your account, and conflicts
articles.summary: Decks reach your account by themselves, and sessions go up when you press Save. This article also covers what happens when two devices disagree.

headings.text: Sessions go up when you press Save

articles.body:
When you're signed in, decks reach your account by themselves, and sessions reach it when you press **Save**. Nothing merges in the background, so you always know which copy is where.

## Decks follow you

Saving a deck on this device also saves it to your account. Your other devices pick it up when you sign in or open the Library's **Decks** tab. If two devices edit the same deck, the last save wins. Deleting a deck that's in your account deletes it from both places.

## Sessions go up when you press Save

While you play, the Dojo saves the session to this device only. **Save** in the top bar also saves it to your account. On a phone, open **⋯** and choose **Save**. If a session is already in your account and has unsaved changes, the Dojo saves it there again when you switch tabs or close the page.

[Show me](show:save)

## Read the Library

In **Sessions**, a row says when its two copies differ:

- **Changed here since your last Save** means this device has changes. Press **Save to account**.
- **Your account has a newer copy** means another device saved later. Press **Get newer copy** to replace this device's copy with it.
- On the **Only in your account** shelf, **Download & open** brings a session to this device.

## When two devices disagree

If the session changed in your account since this device last saved it, **Save** asks **This session changed on another device**. Choose one:

- **Overwrite with mine** makes your account keep this device's version.
- **Save mine as a copy** sends this version to your account as a new session, and the other version stays.
- **Cancel** saves nothing to your account.

## Good to know

- Deleting a session that's in both places asks **This device**, **Account** or **Both**.
- If saving to your account fails, the match is still saved on this device.
- An account holds up to 50 sessions and 200 decks, and a session up to 10 MB compressed.

articles.title: Tweaks
articles.summary: Where the settings are and what each one changes.
articles.body:
Tweaks holds the Dojo's settings. They set how it looks, how big the cards are, and how much it tells you about a challenge.

## Open Tweaks

:::desktop
Press the sliders button at the right end of the top bar. Press it again, or **×**, to close.

[Show me](show:tweaks)
:::

:::phone
Tap **⋯** in the top bar, then **Tweaks**. Tap **×** to close.
:::

Tweaks opens from a match. On the home screen you can only change the theme, with the **Auto / Day / Night** switch at the top.

## What's in it

- **Theme** is **Auto**, **Day** or **Night**. See [Day, night and accent](help:theme).
- **Accent** sets the colour of the main buttons and highlights. See [Day, night and accent](help:theme).
- **Card size** sets how big cards are. See [Card size and Art / Text](help:card-display).
- **Card display** is **Art** or **Text** for every card. See [Card size and Art / Text](help:card-display).
- **Challenge forecast** is **Off**, **Light** or **Full**. See [Challenge forecast](help:forecast).
- **Number keys** is **Off** by default, or **On**. When it's on, number keys pick cards and their menu options. See [Keyboard shortcuts](help:keyboard-shortcuts).
- **Rules engine** is a beta, set to **Off**, **Assist** or **Lab**. See [The rules engine](help:rules-engine).
- **Player palette** is **Competition**, **Modern** or **Mono**. See [Player palette](help:palette).

## Good to know

- A change shows at once, and there's nothing to save.
- This browser keeps your Tweaks. They don't go to your account, and clearing the site's data resets them.

articles.title: Day, night and accent
articles.summary: Follow your device's light or dark setting, or pick Day or Night, and choose the accent colour.
articles.body:
The **Theme** setting picks a light or dark Dojo. **Accent** picks the colour that marks the main button and where you are.

## Choose the theme

In [Tweaks](help:tweaks), **Theme** has three choices:

- **Auto** follows your device's light or dark setting, and changes when it does.
- **Day** always uses the warm light look.
- **Night** always uses the warm dark look.

[Show me](show:tweak-theme)

On the home screen, the **Auto / Day / Night** switch at the top is the same setting.

[Show me](show:home-theme)

## Choose the accent

**Accent** has four swatches. The current one's name shows beside the label.

- **Signal** is the theme's own accent. It's orange by day and a brighter orange at night.
- **Coral**, **Olive** and **Trace** use the same colour in both themes.

The accent colours the main button in each view, like **End turn** and **Start match**. It also colours the marks that show where you are, like the turn number and the line you're on in the Multiverse.

[Show me](show:tweak-accent)

## Good to know

- This browser keeps your choices. The Practice Dojo website follows the same theme.
- The players' colours are a separate setting. See [Player palette](help:palette).

articles.title: Card size and Art / Text
articles.summary: Make cards bigger or smaller, and show card art or text-only cards everywhere.
articles.body:
Two settings in [Tweaks](help:tweaks) change how cards look, **Card size** and **Card display**.

## Card size

Drag the **Card size** slider. It goes from 0.70× to 1.40×, and the value shows beside the label. It starts at 1.00×, or at 0.80× on a touch screen so the board fits a phone.

[Show me](show:tweak-card-size)

When the play area fills up, cards in play still shrink to fit, whatever the setting.

## Art or Text

**Card display** has two choices:

- **Art** shows the card pictures. A card whose picture can't be fetched shows as text instead.
- **Text** shows every card as text, with its name, version, cost, stats and rules. The Dojo loads no card pictures.

[Show me](show:tweak-card-display)

The setting applies everywhere at once, in the board, your hand, the inkwell, the discard, every card grid and the card preview. On a text card, the cost sits in the game's own frame. A winged hexagon means the card is inkable, and a plain hexagon means it isn't. Strength, lore and willpower also use the game's own symbols.

## Good to know

- **Text** needs no pictures, so use it on a slow connection or with none. See [Playing offline](help:offline).
- This browser keeps both settings.

articles.title: Player palette
articles.summary: How the Dojo colours the two players, by their deck's inks, with two fixed colours, or in grey.
articles.body:
**Player palette** in [Tweaks](help:tweaks) sets how the Dojo tells the two players apart by colour.

## Choose a palette

[Show me](show:tweak-palette)

- **Competition** is the default. It shades each side in its own deck's two inks, on the board, the player rows, the lore and the Multiverse nodes. Player 1's mark is split in two, and Player 2's is striped like a barber pole, so you can tell the players apart in a mirror match. Under the switch, a P1 and a P2 icon show the inks it picked. Hover one to see their names. Before both decks are known, it uses Modern's colours.
- **Modern** uses two fixed colours, olive for Player 1 and teal for Player 2, whatever the decks.
- **Mono** uses grey only. There's no colour anywhere, card pictures included. Player 1 is light and Player 2 is heavy.

## Good to know

- The palette only changes the players' colours. The [Theme](help:theme) sets the light or dark look.
- This browser keeps the setting.

articles.title: Challenge forecast
articles.summary: How much the Dojo shows about a challenge before you make it. Pick off, one line, or the full forecast.
articles.body:
**Challenge forecast** sets how much the Dojo tells you about a [challenge](help:challenge) before you make it. The forecast says which cards would be banished and how much damage each card would have.

## Choose how much

In [Tweaks](help:tweaks), **Challenge forecast** has three choices, **Off**, **Light** and **Full**. **Light** is the default.

[Show me](show:tweak-forecast)

:::mouse
The forecast shows while you drag your character onto an opponent's card, or point at one in challenge mode:

- **Off** shows only the arrow.
- **Light** shows one line over the target, with the card that gets banished and the damage after.
- **Full** shows a forecast card with each card's damage before and after, marked **BANISHED** or **SURVIVES**, and the extra damage on both cards. Once you pick an attacker in challenge mode, every opponent card also gets an outcome badge.

The challenge mode bar has the same **Off / Light / Full** switch, so you can change it mid-challenge.

[Show me](show:challenge-banner)
:::

:::touch
A touch screen has no pointer to hover, so **Light** and **Full** work the same way. Once you pick your character in challenge mode, every opponent card gets an outcome badge. **Off** shows no badges.
:::

## Good to know

- The forecast only predicts. The Dojo never stops a challenge. If your character is exerted or drying, the Dojo allows the challenge and says so.
- This browser keeps the setting.

articles.title: The rules engine (beta)
articles.summary: What the rules engine is, how to switch it to Off, Assist or Lab, and what it never does.
articles.body:
The rules engine is an optional helper that knows Lorcana's rules. It runs in your browser, next to the board, and reads the board as you play. It's a **beta**. It misses some cards and situations, and it may change.

The board stays yours. The engine never blocks a move, and you're still the referee, as in [You play both sides](help:you-play-both-sides). Switch it off and the Dojo works as it did before.

## Switch it on

In [Tweaks](help:tweaks), **Rules engine** has three choices:

- **Off** is the default. You get the sandbox with no engine.
- **Assist** marks what the rules allow, suggests plays, can play a seat as a bot, and runs What-if.
- **Lab** adds the score lab to Assist. In the score lab you see and change how the engine scores plays.

[Show me](show:tweak-rules)

The first time you switch it on, the Dojo loads the engine and its card data, about 800 KB. After that it starts at once.

## What it does

- **Marks the legal moves** on the board and lists them in each card's menu. See [What the rules allow](help:rules-assist).
- **Suggests plays** for the rest of the turn and can put one on the board. See [Proposed plays](help:proposed-plays).
- **Plays a seat** as your opponent, one move at a time. See [Play against the bot](help:bot-opponent).
- **Shows the score** behind the suggestions, and in Lab lets you change it. See [The score lab](help:score-lab).
- **Looks for a win you missed** in a game you lost. See [What-if](help:what-if).

## Good to know

- When the engine and the board disagree, the board wins. Fix the board by hand, as you always could.
- The engine only knows what's on the board. It doesn't know which cards were played earlier this turn, except how many you inked. It also doesn't know about an effect that's waiting to be resolved.
- The engine drops an effect that lasts into the next turn when the bot hands a turn back to the board.
- On a phone, a tap on a card opens the card drawer, which has no rules list yet. The marks on the cards still show.
- This browser keeps the setting.

articles.title: What the rules allow
articles.summary: The marks on cards that have a legal move, and the Rules list in a card's menu.

headings.text: The Rules list in a card's menu

articles.body:
With **Rules engine** on **Assist** or **Lab**, the Dojo marks what the rules allow the player whose turn it is. See [The rules engine](help:rules-engine).

## The marks on cards

A card with a legal move gets a ring and a row of small dots under it, one dot per kind of move:

- **Olive** means quest, or put the card in the inkwell.
- **Coral** means challenge.
- **Bone**, a pale dot, means any other move, such as playing the card, singing a song with it, shifting, moving to a location or using an ability.

A card with no legal move has no marks. The marks follow the board. When you change anything, the engine reads the board again.

## The Rules list in a card's menu

:::desktop
Click or right-click a card to open its menu. With the engine on, the menu starts with **Rules**. It shows one of these:

- each legal move, with how many targets it has, like **Challenge · 1 target**.
- for a card in hand that can't be played, the reason, like **Needs 4 ink, 1 ready**.

The list only informs you. The menu's other items work as always, and nothing is blocked.
:::

:::phone
A tap on a card opens the card drawer, which doesn't have the Rules list yet. The marks on the cards still show what's legal.
:::

## Good to know

- The marks are for the player whose turn it is.
- The marks are the engine's reading of the board. If a card does something the engine doesn't know, trust the card and play it by hand.

articles.title: Proposed plays (Suggest)
articles.summary: Ask the engine for the best ways to play the rest of the turn, read why, then play one or keep it as a branch.
articles.body:
With the rules engine on, **Suggest** tries orders of play for the rest of the turn and shows the best lines. Each line says what to play, quest and challenge, the lore it gains, and why it scores.

## Ask for plays

:::desktop
Press **Suggest** beside **Quest**, or the **Plays** tab at the top of the draw odds column. The lines appear in that tab after a few seconds.

[Show me](show:suggest)
:::

:::phone
Tap **☰**, then **Suggest**. The lines open in a **Proposed plays** sheet at the bottom. **×** closes it.
:::

The search plays the board for the player whose turn it is. If the board changes, the lines say so. Press **Search again**, or **↻** at the top, to look again.

## Read a line

Each line has a row with four figures:

- its number.
- the lore it gains, like **+2 lore**.
- the lore after it, like **18–2**.
- its score compared with ending the turn now, like **+4.0**.

Line 1 is open. It lists its steps in order, such as **Play**, **Quest** and **Ink**, with what an ability did under its move. Its **Why** lists the three reasons that moved its score most, like **lore +2.0** and **exposed −1.0**.

The other lines are closed. Each one says how it differs from line 1, as in *Like line 1, but play Strength of a Raging Fire → Prince Phillip instead of play Elinor*. Click or tap a row to open it.

**Show 8 more lines** shows the rest, and its number counts the lines left. The search keeps up to 12 lines.

A red row at the top means ending the turn now loses, because their characters can reach 20 next turn. The row says whether the lines stop that.

:::mouse
Point at a card in a step to see it. Point at an ability for its text, or at a reason or the score for what it means.
:::

## Play it, or keep it

- **Play it** puts the end of the line on the board. It's one step, so **Undo** takes it back. The Dojo writes the turn's recap and log as if you'd played the line.
- **Save as branch** keeps the line as a new node in the [Multiverse](help:branches), without changing the board.

## Good to know

- The score is a guess at how good the board is for you. It counts lore, what's in play, what's exposed to a challenge and the opponent's best reply. [The score lab](help:score-lab) shows the score and lets you change it.
- The search has a time limit. On a busy board it may stop early and say so. The lines are still the best it found.

articles.title: Play against the bot
articles.summary: Let the rules engine play one seat, by itself or one move at a time, and take over whenever you like.
articles.body:
With the rules engine on, the bot can play one seat, P1 or P2, while you play the other. It plays one move at a time, and you can watch, step through or take over.

## Start the bot

:::desktop
Press **Bot** in the top bar.
:::

:::phone
Tap the robot key in the top bar.
:::

[Show me](show:bot)

The menu has three settings:

- **Bot plays** is **Off**, **P1** or **P2**.
- **Pace** is **Auto** or **Step**. **Auto** plays its moves one after another. **Step** waits for you to ask for each one.
- **Speed** sets the pace of **Auto** to **Slow**, **Normal** or **Fast**.

The top bar then says **Bot P2** or **Bot P1**. Your seat stays at the bottom of the board.

## While it plays

A banner shows what the bot is doing, such as **Its turn** or **Thinking…**, and its last move. On desktop the banner sits under the top bar. On a phone it sits at the bottom of the screen, above your Quest and End turn. It has these controls:

- **Auto** and **Step** switch the pace.
- **Pause** in Auto stops the bot. **Next** in Step plays its next move.
- **Take over** switches the bot off so you play its seat yourself.

[Show me](show:bot-banner)

When the bot needs you to choose something during its turn, such as a card of yours that an effect targets, the banner asks you.

:::desktop
{key:P} switches between **Auto** and **Step**, and {key:N} plays the bot's next move.
:::

## Your turn

Play your turn as always, then press **End turn**. The engine runs the turn change, with its start-of-turn and end-of-turn effects, and the bot plays its turn.

## Good to know

- Each bot move is one **Undo** step, and the log says **Bot: …** for each one.
- Switch the bot off at any time. When you switch it on again, it carries on from the board as it is.
- If the bot gets stuck, it pauses and you finish the turn.
- A new game starts with the bot off. So does a game you load from the library, a file, a demo or a Duels.ink import.

articles.title: The score lab
articles.summary: See how the engine scores a board, change the weights, keep profiles, and add your own terms.
articles.body:
The engine ranks [proposed plays](help:proposed-plays) by a score. The score is a number for how good the board is for the player whose turn it is. The score lab shows that score and lets you change it. To switch it on, set **Rules engine** to **Lab** in [Tweaks](help:tweaks). Lab includes everything Assist does.

## The Score tab

:::desktop
Press **Score** at the top of the draw odds column.

[Show me](show:score-tab)

- **Score now** is the score for the player to move.
- **Terms** lists each part of the score. The terms are **lore**, **lore on board** for you and the opponent, **board**, **exposed**, **hand**, **ink**, **race to 20** and **their turn**. Each term has a box to switch it on or off, its weight, and what it's worth on this board now. Type a weight, or click a term's name for a slider. Point at a term to see what it measures.
:::

:::phone
The Score tab is on desktop only, because phones don't have the draw odds column. The card numbers below still show.
:::

## Card numbers

In Lab, each card in play shows its share of the score, like **+1.5** or **−3.7**. The share is what the card adds through lore on board, board and exposed, and through your terms that count cards in play. The numbers follow every change to the board.

:::mouse
Point at a number for the sum behind it, like *lore on board 2 × 0.6 = +1.20*.
:::

## Profiles

A profile is a set of weights and terms, kept in this browser. The list at the top of the Score tab picks the one in use.

- **Default** holds the engine's own weights. It never changes. If you edit it, you get a draft called **Default · edited**. Press **Save** to keep the draft as a new profile.
- **⋯** has **Save as…**, **Rename**, **Delete**, **Undo edits**, **Export** to a file, and **Import**.

With a profile other than Default, each proposed line shows **↑** or **↓** compared with where Default ranked it. The open line lists **All terms** with what each one changed. Changing the weights marks the lines as old, so press **Search again**.

## Your own terms

Under **Your terms**, **+ New term** adds a part of your own to the score. A term has these settings:

- **Whose** cards, mine or theirs, and **Where** they are, in play, in hand, in the inkwell or in the discard.
- Filters for **Type**, **Keyword**, **Class**, **State**, **Can**, **Does**, **Cost** and **Named**. **State** is ready, exerted or damaged. **Can** is quest or challenge. **Does** is what the card's abilities do, such as draw, removal, ramp or lore. **Cost** takes a range.
- A **Measure**, which is how many, lore, strength, willpower left or cost.
- A **Weight**.
- **When**, which is **Always**, or only when **Ahead** or **Behind** in the race.

The form shows what the term is worth on this board and rings the cards it counts. A term that looks at cards the opponent holds or inked is marked **peeks**. It uses information the Dojo shows you that the real game would hide.

## Good to know

- This browser keeps your profiles. Export one to keep it or move it to another device.
- The score is a guess, tuned by play against the engine's own bot. A higher score doesn't promise a win.

articles.title: What-if: find a win you missed
articles.summary: Play a lost game out again from your turns before the loss, looking for a line that would have won.

headings.text: What it does at each turn back
Games that fork, or aren't finished

articles.body:
What-if takes a game you lost and plays it out again from your turns before the loss, one turn back at a time, looking for a line that would have won. Each line it plays becomes a branch in the [Multiverse](help:multiverse), so you can open it and play from it.

What-if needs the rules engine on **Assist** or **Lab**. See [The rules engine](help:rules-engine). It also needs a game saved turn by turn. That can be an [imported Duels.ink replay](help:import-replay) or [text log](help:import-log), or a game played here with [auto-save](help:auto-save) on.

## Start it

Open the [Multiverse](help:multiverse) and press **What-if** in its header. On a phone it's the key left of **Plot**. The What-if block opens at the top of the panel.

[Show me](show:what-if)

:::desktop
The **What-if** key in the mini Multiverse's header also opens it.
:::

Press **Look for a win**. It takes about half a minute for each turn back. A dot pulses on **What-if** and on **Multiverse** while it runs, and **Stop** ends it.

## What it does at each turn back

What-if starts at your last turn before the loss and goes back one of your turns at a time, up to 5 turns. At each one it plays these lines:

1. **The real game, replayed.** It replays both players' real moves from that turn, which should end as the real game did. The panel then says *The real game replays as it ended*. Sometimes the replay doesn't match, because of a card the engine can't see or a move it can't make. What-if then still tries that turn, and compares the lines with What you did as the engine plays it, not with the real game.
2. **What you did.** It plays your real move, with the search playing your later turns. This line must still lose.
3. **Lines 1 to 4.** It plays the search's four best other ways to play that turn, each to the end.

On your later turns, What-if plays the search's best line. On the opponent's turns, it plays their real moves and then lets the search finish their turn, unless the search finds a clearly better move. It stops at the first turn back with a winning line.

## Read the results

[Show me](show:what-if-panel)

- Each turn back has a row, like **3 back · Turn 19**, and a badge that reads **Win** or **No win**. For an unfinished game, the badge reads **Better** or **Not better**.
- **What you did** and each line show the lore at the end, like **19–20**, whether the line **Wins** or **Loses** and on which turn, and its moves.
- A win shows in Olive. The opponent's lore reaching 20 shows in Coral.
- **Show** selects the line's last node in the Multiverse.
- **Keep going** looks further back. **Remove 9 losing lines** takes the losing branches out of the Multiverse, and its number counts them. The toast's **Undo** puts them back.

## Games that fork, or aren't finished

- A game with more than one line, or one that isn't finished, asks where to start. Select a turn in the Multiverse, then press **Start from turn N**. **Pick another start** goes back.
- What-if plays an unfinished game to 2 turns past its last turn and compares the lore race, your lore minus theirs, instead of who wins. **Better** marks a line that beats What you did.
- A game played here has no record of the opponent's moves. What-if doesn't replay the real game, the search plays the opponent's turns, and What you did is the real board after your turn, played on.

## Good to know

- What-if is a beta, and the opponent's side is its weak point. A "win" can come from the search not using one of their cards the way a person would. Open the branch and check it.
- The branches stay in the session. The results in the panel last while the page is open. A reload or another game starts What-if afresh.

articles.title: Playing offline and missing card art
articles.summary: Card names and text still show when art can't load, and this browser keeps the card database for offline starts.
articles.body:
Card pictures come from the internet. When one can't load, the card shows as text instead, so you can still read the board and keep playing.

## When art doesn't load

A card without its picture shows its name, version, ink cost, strength and willpower. Its full text is in the preview on desktop and in the card drawer on a phone. Face-down cards and the deck show plain dark.

Pictures come back when your connection does. Pictures that loaded once in a session stay loaded, even if the connection drops later.

## Text cards on purpose

In **Tweaks**, set **Card display** to **Text**. Every card then shows as text, and the Dojo loads no card pictures. Use it on a slow or metered connection.

[Show me](show:tweak-card-display)

## Starting without a connection

After the first visit, the Dojo keeps a copy of the card database in this browser, so it can start without downloading it again. The first visit needs a connection. Without one you see *Error loading database. Please refresh.*

The Dojo isn't an installed app. Once it's open you can play offline. Reopening it with no connection works only if your browser still has its files cached.

## Good to know

- The Dojo saves your sessions and decks in this browser, so they don't need a connection. See [Where your things are kept](help:storage).
- Making a share link, opening a link and signing in need a connection.

articles.title: Where your things are kept, and how to lose them
articles.summary: Sessions and decks live in this browser unless you sign in. Clearing site data deletes them.
articles.body:
The Dojo saves your sessions and decks in this browser, on this device. No Dojo server holds them unless you sign in.

## What deletes them

- **Clearing this site's data** deletes every session and deck saved here. Browsers call this clearing cookies and site data, or browsing data.
- **Another browser or device** has its own, separate library. Chrome and Firefox on the same computer don't share one.
- **A private window** may not keep anything after it closes, or may not let the Dojo save at all. The Library then says *This browser isn't letting the Dojo keep a library (private window?).*
- **The browser itself** may clear storage when the device runs short of space. When you save, the Dojo asks the browser to keep its storage, but the browser decides.

If a save fails, the Dojo says *Couldn't save to this device. Export the session to keep it.*

## How to keep them

- **Export a file.** In the Library, open a session's **⋯** menu and choose **Export file (.dojo.json.gz)**. Keep the file anywhere. **Import file** opens it again. See [Export and import session files](help:files).
- **Sign in.** Decks follow your account by themselves, and a session goes to your account when you press **Save**. See [Why sign in](help:account).

[Show me](show:library)

## Good to know

- The Library sorts everything by where it lives, under *On this device*, *Only on this device* and *In your account + this device*.
- Your share links also belong to this browser. If you clear its data, the links keep working for everyone, but you can no longer list or delete them. Signing in first keeps them in your account.
- This browser also keeps your **Tweaks** choices.

articles.title: Shortcuts don't do anything
articles.summary: Why a keyboard shortcut might not fire, such as typing in a field, an open dialog, or the home screen.

headings.text: A dialog, the mulligan or the home screen is in front

articles.body:
The Dojo ignores its shortcuts whenever a key could mean something else. Check these causes, in order.

## You're typing in a field

While the cursor is in a text field, keys type letters. Text fields include the session title, the turn notes box, the paste field and the search boxes. Click an empty part of the board, or press {key:Tab} to leave the field. In the session title, {key:Enter} keeps the name and leaves the field.

## A dialog, the mulligan or the home screen is in front

- **A dialog is open.** Only its own {key:Enter} and {key:Esc} work. Answer it first.
- **The mulligan is up.** No shortcut works until you choose **Keep hand** or **Mulligan**, so {key:Space} can't end the turn by accident.
- **The home screen is in front.** Game keys never act on the board hidden behind it. {key:Esc} takes you back to your match, if one is on the board.

## A card key does nothing

{key:E}, {key:B}, {key:0} to {key:9} and the damage keys need the pointer over a card in play. Nothing can be open over the board, such as the Multiverse, **Inspect deck** or a card search. The keys also don't work while challenge mode is on. Press {key:Esc} or **Done** to leave it.

With **Number keys** on in [Tweaks](help:tweaks), {key:1} to {key:9} on their own pick a card in your hand. {key:B} then a number picks a card on your battlefield. Move the pointer off the cards in play first, or those keys go to the card under it.

## Space pressed a button

If you just clicked a button, it keeps the focus, and {key:Space} presses it again instead of ending the turn. Click an empty part of the board first.

## Good to know

- The Dojo leaves Ctrl, Cmd and Alt combinations to the browser, so {key:Ctrl+Z} doesn't undo. Press {key:U} or **Undo** in the top bar.
- The mini multiverse's arrow keys need the map to have focus. Click it first.
- Phones have no shortcuts. See [Touch gestures](help:gestures).

articles.title: Share link limits
articles.summary: How many links you can make, how big a session can be, and what the messages mean.
articles.body:
Share links are free and need no account. The Dojo sets a few limits to keep them that way. Opening a link has no limits.

## The limits

- **20 links a day and 100 in total.** The limits apply per browser, or per account once you sign in. Both count the links you still have, so deleting old ones in the Library's **Links** tab frees room. The day is the last 24 hours.
- **10 MB per session, compressed.** A deck link holds only the list.
- **Shared storage.** When the Dojo's shared storage fills up, sharing sessions pauses for everyone. Deck links still work.

[Show me](show:lib-links)

## What the messages mean

- *You've reached the sharing limit: 20 links a day and 100 in total.* Delete links you no longer need, or wait.
- *This session is N MB compressed, and shared sessions can be up to 10 MB.* Delete auto-saves or dead-end branches in the Multiverse, then share again.
- *Sharing sessions is paused because the Dojo's shared storage is full.* You can't fix this one. Share the deck, or send the file instead. See [Export and import session files](help:files).
- *Too many new sharers from this network in the last hour.* The first link from a browser sets it up for sharing, and the Dojo limits that per network. Try again later.
- *This browser can't compress session files, so it can't share them.* Use a current browser.
- *Couldn't reach the sharing service.* Check your connection.
- **This share is no longer available** means the person who made the link deleted it.

## Good to know

- A link is a snapshot. Later changes to your session aren't in it, so share again to send them.

articles.title: Browsers and devices
articles.summary: Which browsers the Dojo runs in, and what changes on a phone or tablet.
articles.body:
The Dojo runs in the browser, so there's nothing to install. Use a current Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari, on a computer, tablet or phone.

## What the browser needs

- **Storage.** The Dojo keeps your sessions, your decks and the card database in IndexedDB. Some private windows block it, and then nothing is kept. See [Where your things are kept](help:storage).
- **Compression.** Session files and share links need it. Without it, the Dojo still saves on the device, but it can't share a session or open a `.gz` file.
- **A connection the first time.** The Dojo downloads the card database on the first visit. See [Playing offline](help:offline).

## Phone, tablet or computer

The layout follows the width of the window, and the controls follow how you point.

- **760 pixels wide or less** gets the phone layout. It has one player bar per player, your hand along the bottom, the card drawer, the **⋯** menu and the Multiverse's thumb keys. It has no mini multiverse or draw odds column.
- **Wider** gets the desktop layout, with the side rail holding the mini multiverse, the preview, the log and the draw odds.
- **A mouse** gets hover controls on cards, right-click menus and [keyboard shortcuts](help:keyboard-shortcuts).
- **A touch screen** gets taps instead. A tap on a card in play opens the card drawer. See [Touch gestures](help:gestures).

A tablet gets the desktop layout with touch. Turning a phone sideways, or zooming the browser, can change the layout.

## Good to know

- Each browser keeps its own library. Sessions saved in Safari don't show up in Chrome. Sign in to have them in both.

articles.title: Keyboard shortcuts
articles.summary: Every key the Dojo listens to, on the board, on a card, in the Multiverse and in dialogs.

headings.text: On a card under the pointer

articles.body:
This page lists every key the Dojo answers to, grouped by where it works. Keys are single presses. The Dojo leaves anything with Ctrl, Cmd or Alt to your browser. If a key does nothing, see [Shortcuts don't do anything](help:hotkeys-not-working).

## Anywhere on the board

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| {key:Space} | **End turn**. If a button has focus, Space presses that button instead |
| {key:U} | **Undo** the last action, like **Undo** in the top bar |
| {key:Q} | **Quest** with every ready character of the active player that has lore and isn't drying |
| {key:M} | Open or close the **Multiverse** |
| {key:T} | **Save current unfinished turn**. It opens the Multiverse with the form, ready for you to type the name |
| {key:C} | Turn **Challenge** mode on or off |
| {key:Esc} | Close the innermost thing that's open. The order is below |

**Esc** closes one thing at a time, in this order:

1. a card's menu
2. the card drawer
3. the inkwell sheet
4. a picked ink card
5. the picked challenger
6. challenge mode
7. the Multiverse
8. the Library
9. the home screen, which takes you back to your match if one is on the board
10. a card you're looking at in the mulligan
11. **Inspect deck**, **Inspect discard**, the log import window or the card search

## Number keys

**Number keys** starts off. Turn it on in [Tweaks](help:tweaks) first. Then these keys work:

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| {key:1} to {key:9} | Open the menu of that card in your hand, counting from the left |
| {key:B} then {key:1} to {key:9} | Open the menu of that card on your battlefield, in the order on screen |
| {key:H} | Go back to your hand, so the next {key:1} to {key:9} picks a card in it. {key:B} and {key:H} close a card's open menu |

The picked card shows in the card inspector.

## On a card under the pointer

Point at a card in play, on either side, and press one of these keys:

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| {key:+} or {key:=} | Add 1 damage |
| {key:-} | Remove 1 damage |
| {key:0} to {key:9} | Set the damage to that number |
| {key:E} | Exert or ready |
| {key:B} | Banish to the discard |
| {key:C} | Open challenge mode with this character picked as the challenger. It must be one of the active player's characters |

These keys work only while no window is open over the board, and not in challenge mode. The card's menu shows the same keys beside **Exert**, **Challenge…** and **Banish**. With the pointer over a card in play, {key:0} to {key:9} and {key:B} act on that card instead of picking one.

## In a card's menu

With **Number keys** on, the menu numbers its first nine options.

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| {key:1} to {key:9} | Choose that option |
| {key:↑} {key:↓} | Move through the options |
| {key:←} {key:→} | Open the previous or next card's menu, in your hand or on your battlefield |
| {key:Esc} | Close the menu |

## In challenge mode

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| {key:←} {key:→} | Go to the previous or next card on the side you're on. The first arrow picks your first ready character |
| {key:↑} {key:↓} | Go to the row above or below. {key:↑} off your top row moves to the opponent's cards, and {key:↓} off theirs comes back |
| {key:Enter} | Challenge the card you're aiming at |
| {key:Esc} | Drop the picked challenger, then leave challenge mode |

[Read more](help:challenge)

## A card with keyboard focus

Press {key:Tab} to move through the cards.

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| {key:Enter} or {key:Space} | Open the card's menu. In challenge mode, pick the card or challenge it |
| {key:↑} {key:↓} | Move through the menu's items |
| {key:Enter} | Choose the item |
| {key:Esc} | Close the menu |

The cards in the discard list beside the board open their menu the same way.

## With the bot playing

These keys work while the [bot](help:bot-opponent) plays a seat:

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| {key:P} | Switch the bot between **Auto** and **Step** |
| {key:N} | Play the bot's next move |

## Card drawer

On a touch screen with a keyboard, such as a tablet, the card drawer takes these keys:

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| {key:←} {key:→} | Go to the previous or next card, in the hand or in play on that card's side |
| {key:Esc} | Close the drawer |

## Multiverse

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| {key:←} | Select the turn before, which is the node's parent |
| {key:→} | Select the turn after, which is the node's first child |
| {key:↑} {key:↓} | Select the branch above or below, which is the next node that grows from the same parent |
| {key:Enter} | **Play from here**, which loads the selected node |
| {key:T} | **Save current unfinished turn** |
| {key:M} or {key:Esc} | Close the Multiverse |

With the mouse, drag the canvas to pan, scroll to zoom, and double-click a node to play from it.

These keys work while you edit in the panel:

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| {key:Enter} or {key:Space} on the note | Start editing the note |
| {key:Enter} in a node's name | Save the name |
| {key:Ctrl+Enter} in a note | Save the note. On a Mac, press {key:Cmd+Enter}. Clicking away also saves |
| {key:Esc} in a name or note | Cancel the edit |
| {key:Enter} in the save form's **Name** | **Save node** |
| {key:Esc} in the save form | Close the form |

[Show me](show:tree-canvas)

## Mini multiverse

Click the map or one of its step keys first, so it has focus. Then these keys work:

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| {key:←} | Go to the previous turn |
| {key:→} | Go to the next turn on this line |
| {key:↑} {key:↓} | Go to the line above or below |
| {key:Home} | Go back to the last branch point, or the start |
| {key:End} | Go on to the next branch point, or the line's end |

Click a dot to load it. Drag or scroll the map to pan.

[Show me](show:mini-multiverse-keys)

## Menus and dialogs

| Where | Key | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Dialogs | {key:Enter} | Confirm with the main button |
| Dialogs | {key:Esc} | Cancel |
| A note dialog, like **Turn N notes** | {key:Enter} | Start a new line |
| A note dialog | {key:Ctrl+Enter} or {key:Cmd+Enter} | Save |
| Session title | {key:Enter} | Keep the new name |
| Session title | {key:Esc} | Put the old name back |
| Library tabs | {key:←} {key:→} | Switch between **Sessions**, **Decks** and **Links** |
| A Library row's **⋯** menu | {key:↑} {key:↓} {key:Home} {key:End} | Move through the items |
| A Library row's **⋯** menu | {key:Esc} or {key:Tab} | Close the menu. Esc closes the menu before the Library |
| Inkwell | {key:Esc} | Put down a picked ink card |
| Mulligan | {key:Esc} | Put back a card you're looking at. The mulligan itself stays until you settle the hand |

While a dialog is open, the board's keys do nothing.

## Help

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| {key:?} | Open or close help, except while you're typing |
| {key:/} | Jump to the help search |
| {key:↑} {key:↓} | Move through the search results |
| {key:Enter} | Open the result |
| {key:Esc} | Clear the search, then go back from an article, then close help |
| {key:Backspace} in an empty search | Go back from an article to the contents |

## Good to know

- **Q** and **Space** still act on the board while the Multiverse is open. They quest and end the turn on the board behind it.
- A phone has no shortcuts. See [Touch gestures](help:gestures).

articles.title: Touch gestures
articles.summary: Every tap, hold, swipe and drag on a phone or tablet.
articles.body:
This page lists every gesture the Dojo answers to. Most are taps that open the card drawer. The rest are holds, swipes and drags.

## Cards

| Gesture | Where | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| {gesture:tap} | A card in play | Opens the card drawer with damage, **Challenge**, **Quest**, **Exert**, **Banish** and the moves |
| {gesture:tap} | A card in your hand, on a phone | Opens the card drawer for it, with **Play**, **Ink**, **Discard** and more |
| {gesture:swipe} | Sideways on the card text in the drawer | Shows the next card when you swipe left, or the previous one when you swipe right |
| {gesture:tap} | Outside the drawer | Closes the drawer |
| {gesture:drag} | A card from your hand, up | Plays it onto the field, inks it onto the ink count, or shifts it onto a matching character |
| {gesture:drag} | Any card you can pick up | Moves it onto the discard, the deck or a hand |

:::desktop touch
On a tablet, a tap on a card in your hand opens its menu instead of the drawer.
:::

[Show me](show:card-drawer)

## Challenge

| Gesture | What it does |
|---|---|
| {gesture:tap} **Challenge** | Turns challenge mode on |
| {gesture:tap} your character, then an opponent's card | Challenges that card |
| {gesture:drag} your character onto an opponent's card | Also challenges that card |
| {gesture:tap} the arrow keys, then the fist | Picks your character, swaps to aim at a target, and challenges it |
| {gesture:tap} the bare battlefield | Leaves challenge mode |

## The board

| Gesture | Where | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| {gesture:long-press} | The empty battlefield, for about half a second | Opens **Turn N notes** for the active player |
| {gesture:tap} | The ink count | Opens the inkwell sheet, where you spend and ready ink, press **Ready all** or act on each ink card |
| {gesture:tap} | The deck | Draws a card |
| {gesture:tap} | **⋮** on the deck | Opens the deck actions, inspect and shuffle |
| {gesture:tap} | The magnifier on the discard | Opens the discard |
| {gesture:tap} | **Hold to reveal hand** | Shows the other player's hand. Tap again to hide it |
| {gesture:tap} | **−** or **+** by the lore | Changes the lore by one |
| {gesture:tap} | **Quest** by your hand | Quests with every ready character |
| {gesture:tap} | **End turn** by your hand | Ends the turn |

Moving your finger cancels a long press, so scrolling never opens the notes.

[Show me](show:turn-notes)

## Mulligan

| Gesture | What it does |
|---|---|
| {gesture:tap} a card | Marks it to go to the bottom. Tap again to keep it |
| {gesture:long-press} a card | Shows it large with its name, cost and type. It stays when you lift your finger |
| {gesture:tap} anywhere | Closes the large card. That tap marks nothing |

## Multiverse

| Gesture | What it does |
|---|---|
| {gesture:tap} a node or dot | Selects it, and the panel shows it |
| {gesture:tap} **Play from here** | Loads the selected node |
| {gesture:drag} the canvas | Pans |
| {gesture:pinch} | Zooms in or out |
| {gesture:tap} ◀ or ▶ | Goes to the turn before or after |
| {gesture:tap} ▲ or ▼ | Goes to another line |
| {gesture:tap} ◎ | Goes back to where you are |
| {gesture:tap} zoom out | Shows the whole game, in the plot only |
| {gesture:long-press} an arrow key | Keeps stepping, like holding a key |

[Show me](show:tree-keys)

## Menus

- {gesture:tap} **☰** for the side rail, with the players, the game log and **Auto-save every turn**.
- {gesture:tap} **⋯** for **Save**, **Save as copy**, **Share link**, **Tweaks** and **Leave to the dojo**. Tap outside to close it.

articles.title: Glossary
articles.summary: Dojo words such as node, line, branch and Left here, and the Lorcana terms the manual uses.
articles.body:
This page defines the words the manual uses, first the Dojo's own and then Lorcana's.

## Dojo words

- **Session.** One match and everything saved from it, with the board, its Multiverse and its history. The Dojo saves it as you play. [Sessions](help:sessions)
- **Multiverse.** The tree of every saved turn in a session. [The Multiverse](help:multiverse)
- **Node.** One saved board in the Multiverse. It shows whose turn it is, the lore, a note and what happened. [Reading a node](help:nodes)
- **Line.** A run of turns, one after another, from the start to where it ends.
- **Branch.** A line that splits off an earlier node, when you play from there and do something different. [Branching](help:branches)
- **The line you're on.** The line that leads to the board in front of you. The Dojo marks it, and the node you're on, in the signal colour.
- **Auto-save.** With **Auto-save every turn** on, every turn gets a node. The node holds the board the turn starts from, and gets the turn's note and recap once it ends. [Every turn is saved](help:auto-save)
- **Left here.** A dashed snapshot of a board you jumped away from before saving it. [Left here snapshots](help:left-here)
- **Library.** Your sessions, decks and links, on shelves by where they're kept. The shelves are this device, your account, built in and public links. [The Library](help:library)
- **Share link.** A short link to a frozen copy of a deck or a session. Anyone with the link can open it. [Share a deck or a session](help:share-links)
- **Rules engine.** An optional beta helper that knows Lorcana's rules. It marks legal moves, suggests plays, plays a seat as a bot and runs What-if. It never blocks a move. [The rules engine](help:rules-engine)
- **Proposed plays.** The best lines for the rest of the turn that **Suggest** finds. Each line shows the lore it gains and why it scores. [Proposed plays](help:proposed-plays)
- **What-if.** A lost game played out again from your turns before the loss, looking for a line that would have won. [What-if](help:what-if)
- **Practice board.** The board a guided tour runs on. Nothing on it is saved, and your own match stays as it was. [Guided tours](help:tours)
- **Unknown card.** A card an imported game never showed. It reads **Unknown card** until you fill it in. [Unknown cards](help:unknown-cards)

## Lorcana words

- **Ink, inkwell.** Cards put face down to pay for other cards. Each ink pays 1, once a turn. [Ink a card](help:ink-a-card)
- **Ready, exert.** A ready card stands upright. Exerting turns it sideways, to quest, challenge or pay for an ability. [Act on a card](help:card-actions)
- **Quest.** Exert a character to gain its lore. [Quest and lore](help:quest)
- **Lore.** The score. The first player to reach 20 wins. [Winning](help:winning)
- **Challenge.** Exert your character to fight an exerted opposing character or a location. Each card deals damage equal to its strength to the other. [Challenge](help:challenge)
- **Banish.** Put a card from play into its owner's discard, for example when its damage reaches its willpower.
- **Drying.** A character played this turn can't quest or challenge yet. The board marks it **NEW**.
- **Shift.** Play a character on top of another version of it, for its shift cost. The card underneath stays under it. [Locations, shift and cards under](help:locations-and-stacks)
- **Singer, song.** A character can exert to sing a song instead of paying its ink. The Dojo doesn't track singing, so exert the singer and play the song yourself.
- **Location.** A card your characters can move to. It has willpower and can give lore. [Locations](help:locations-and-stacks)

The Dojo doesn't enforce Lorcana's rules. You're the referee.

text.desktop: This is a practice board with two ready-made decks. Nothing you do here is saved. **Leave any time with ✕ or Esc.**
text.phone: This is a practice board with two ready-made decks. Nothing you do here is saved. **Leave any time with ✕.**

text.desktop: First, your opening hand. **Click the magnifier** in a card's top-right corner to look at it up close. **Click again** to put it back.
text.phone: First, your opening hand. **Press and hold a card** to see it large. **Tap anywhere on it** to put it back.

text.desktop: **Click a card you don't want**, say the most expensive one, to send it to the bottom. The curve and inkable readout under the hand show what you'd keep. Click it again to keep it.
text.phone: **Tap a card you don't want**, say the most expensive one, to send it to the bottom. The readout under the hand shows what you'd keep. Tap it again to keep it.

text.desktop: **Press Mulligan.** The key counts the cards you marked. They go to the bottom of your deck, you draw as many, and the Dojo shuffles the deck. With nothing marked, the key says Keep hand.
text.phone: **Tap Mulligan.** The key counts the cards you marked. They go to the bottom of your deck, you draw as many, and the Dojo shuffles the deck. With nothing marked, the key says Keep hand.

text.desktop: This is your new hand. The card you drew has a NEW pip. **Press Start turn** to play.
text.phone: This is your new hand. The card you drew has a NEW pip. **Tap Start turn** to play.

steps.text: The bottom half belongs to the player whose turn it is. It holds their hand, play area and inkwell. The other player's side is at the top.

text.desktop: Put a card in your inkwell. **Drag it from your hand onto the inkwell**, or **click it and press Add to the Inkwell**.
text.phone: Put a card in your inkwell. **Drag it from your hand onto the inkwell**, or **tap a card in your hand, then Ink**.

hint.phone: Only inkable cards can be inked. The others say **No ink**.

text.desktop: Now play a card. **Drag a 1-cost character onto your play area**, or **click it and press Play Card**.
text.phone: Now play a card. **Drag a 1-cost character onto your play area**, or **tap a 1-cost character, then Play**.

steps.hint: The cost is the number in the card's top-left corner.

steps.text: **Hover any card on the board** to read it here at full size, with its cost, strength, willpower, lore and text.
**Tap a card in your hand** to open its drawer. It shows the card at full size and what you can do with it. **Close it** when you've read it.

text.desktop: When you're done for this turn, **press End turn** or the Space bar.
text.phone: When you're done for this turn, **tap End turn**.

steps.text: Now you're Player 2. The board turns round, so their side is at the bottom. **Settle their opening hand, then ink one of their cards.**

text.desktop: Undo takes back the last thing you did. **Press Undo** now to take that ink back.
text.phone: Undo takes back the last thing you did. **Tap Undo** now to take that ink back.

steps.text: The Dojo keeps every turn you end as a node in the Multiverse. The mini map shows them here. **Press Multiverse or M** to open the whole tree.
The Dojo keeps every turn you end as a node in the Multiverse. **Tap this button** to open the whole tree.

text.desktop: This is a game in progress, on your turn 9. The Dojo moves the cards and keeps the score, but **it doesn't read the cards**. Nothing checks a card's text, its keywords or what it lets you choose. You do, as you would across a real table. **Leave any time with ✕ or Esc.**
text.phone: This is a game in progress, on your turn 9. The Dojo moves the cards and keeps the score, but **it doesn't read the cards**. Nothing checks a card's text, its keywords or what it lets you choose. You do, as you would across a real table. **Leave any time with ✕.**

text.desktop: Your hand holds **The Horseman Strikes!**, which says "Draw a card. You may banish chosen character with Evasive." **Play it. Drag it onto your play area**, or **click it and press Play Card**. The Dojo spends its 3 ink for you.
text.phone: Your hand holds **The Horseman Strikes!**, which says "Draw a card. You may banish chosen character with Evasive." **Play it. Tap it in your hand, then Play.** The Dojo spends its 3 ink for you.

text.desktop: Nothing happened, because you carry out the card's effects. It says draw a card, so **click your deck to draw one**.
text.phone: Nothing happened, because you carry out the card's effects. It says draw a card, so **tap your deck to draw one**.

text.desktop: Now "banish chosen character with Evasive". Which of their characters has Evasive? The Dojo won't tell you, and it won't stop you choosing wrong. **Hover their cards to read them, then banish the one with Evasive.** Hover it and press Banish, or press B.
text.phone: Now "banish chosen character with Evasive". Which of their characters has Evasive? The Dojo won't tell you, and it won't stop you choosing wrong. **Tap their cards to read them, then banish the one with Evasive** with Banish in its drawer.

steps.hint: It's **Vixey**. Evasive is the first word of her text.

wrong.text: The Dojo let you, but that character doesn't have Evasive. Across a real table your opponent would stop you. Here, you're the referee. **Press Undo**, then banish the one with Evasive.

text.desktop: An action stays in play until you put it away. **Send The Horseman Strikes! to your discard. Hover it and press Banish**, or drag it onto your discard pile.
text.phone: An action stays in play until you put it away. **Send The Horseman Strikes! to your discard. Tap it, then Banish.**

steps.text: Now a longer play. You have **6 ink**, Peter Pan and Luisa are ready, and Elinor is in your way. Here is the plan. Quest with Luisa. Use **Magical Maneuvers** to exert Elinor and take Luisa back to your hand. Then shift **Peter Pan & Tinker Bell** onto Peter Pan and challenge Elinor.

text.desktop: **Quest with Luisa Madrigal. Hover her and press the quest lore gem**, or right-click her and choose Quest.
text.phone: **Quest with Luisa Madrigal. Tap her, then Quest.**

text.desktop: **Play Magical Maneuvers** for 2 ink. Drag it onto your play area, or click it and press Play Card. It says "Return chosen character of yours to your hand. Exert chosen character."
text.phone: **Play Magical Maneuvers** for 2 ink. Tap it in your hand, then Play. It says "Return chosen character of yours to your hand. Exert chosen character."

text.desktop: As before, the Dojo doesn't put an action away for you. **Send Magical Maneuvers to your discard yourself.** Hover it and press Banish, or drag it onto your discard pile.
text.phone: As before, the Dojo doesn't put an action away for you. **Send Magical Maneuvers to your discard yourself. Tap it, then Banish.**

text.desktop: Now carry out its effects, one at a time. For "Exert chosen character", **exert Elinor. Hover her and press Exert**, or press E.
text.phone: Now carry out its effects, one at a time. For "Exert chosen character", **exert Elinor. Tap her, then Exert.**

text.desktop: For "Return chosen character of yours to your hand", **right-click Luisa and choose Return to Hand**, or drag her onto your hand. The lore she quested for stays.
text.phone: For "Return chosen character of yours to your hand", **tap Luisa, then To hand.** The lore she quested for stays.

args.card: Peter Pan & Tinker Bell - Fast Friends

text.desktop: **Shift Peter Pan & Tinker Bell onto Peter Pan. Drag it from your hand onto Peter Pan.** The Dojo spends its Shift cost of 4 ink for you. It takes Peter Pan's place, ready and dry.
text.phone: **Shift Peter Pan & Tinker Bell onto Peter Pan. Press it in your hand and drag it onto Peter Pan.** The Dojo spends its Shift cost of 4 ink for you. It takes Peter Pan's place, ready and dry.

args.card: Peter Pan & Tinker Bell - Fast Friends

text.desktop: Elinor is exerted, so she can be challenged. **Drag Peter Pan & Tinker Bell onto Elinor** to challenge her. The forecast shows how it ends before you let go.
text.phone: Elinor is exerted, so she can be challenged. **Drag Peter Pan & Tinker Bell onto Elinor** to challenge her, or tap it, press Challenge, then tap Elinor.

steps.hint: The Dojo would let you challenge a ready character too, or one with Evasive. You keep to the rules.

steps.text: Some cards change lore directly. **A Pirate's Life** says "Each opponent loses 2 lore. You gain 2 lore." Nothing does that for you. **Press + or − beside a player's Lore** to set it, at any time, for any card that asks.
This is a practice copy of the Set 14 demo. It holds a whole game, with the other ways it could have gone. Nothing you do here is saved.

text.desktop: **Open the Multiverse. Press it, or press M.**
text.phone: **Open the Multiverse. Tap it.**

steps.text: Every node is a saved turn. It shows whose turn it was, the lore, and what they played. Turns run left to right. Where a line forks, the game went another way.

text.desktop: **Click a node** to select it. The arrow keys also step through the tree.
text.phone: **Tap a node** to select it.

steps.text: The panel shows the selected node. **Press Play from here** to put that board back on the table.

hint.desktop: Double-clicking a node, or pressing Enter, does the same.

steps.text: **Now play it differently.** Try a new card or another challenge. When you end the turn, the Multiverse keeps both lines. That fork is a branch.

text.desktop: To keep a turn before it's over, **press T**, or **Save current unfinished turn** in the Multiverse, **then Save node**.
text.phone: To keep a turn before it's over, **open the Multiverse, tap Save current unfinished turn, then Save node**.

text.desktop: Plot shows every saved turn as a dot, so a long game fits on one screen. **Press Plot.**
text.phone: Plot switches between dots and cards. **Tap Plot.**

steps.text: The thumb keys step through the tree. ◀ and ▶ go to the turn before and after. ▲ and ▼ go to the line above and below. The circle goes back to where you are.
**Close the Multiverse with ✕** to go back to the board.
On the board, the mini map keeps the tree in view. **Click a dot** to go there, or **step with its keys**.
**Paste a Duels.ink log or replay into this field**, or **drop the file on the page**. The Dojo works out what it is.

text.desktop: To try it without a game of your own, **press A Duels.ink log** for an example.
text.phone: To try it without a game of your own, **tap A Duels.ink log** for an example.

steps.text: The readout says what it found, a Duels.ink log and how many turns it has.

text.desktop: **Press Study this game.** In the tour it opens as a practice board, so nothing goes in your library.
text.phone: **Tap Study this game.** In the tour it opens as a practice board, so nothing goes in your library.

steps.text: Every turn of the game is now a node. **Open the Multiverse** to see them.
Here's the game turn by turn. **Select a node and press Play from here** to replay it. Cards the log never names stay unknown until you fill them in.
